data.title: Reading NFC Passport Chips in Linux
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary:
文章描述了如何使用Linux系统读取护照NFC芯片中的数据，重点介绍了利用Python脚本重建机器可读区（MRZ）作为NFC芯片密码的过程。护照的NFC芯片受密码保护，密码由护照号码、出生日期和到期日组成，每个数据段都有校验码。由于作废护照的MRZ部分被剪掉，文章提供了生成MRZ的Python代码，利用已知的护照信息计算出完整的密码。

文章还探讨了护照NFC芯片的安全性，指出由于芯片没有计时器，无法记录读取次数，理论上可以通过暴力破解尝试密码。尽管破解过程可能需要几天时间，但并非不可能。此外，文章提到大多数NFC芯片支持无限次读取，这增加了被破解的风险。最终，文章提醒用户护照的安全性依赖于物理和密码学的多重保护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器可读旅行证件（Machine Readable Travel Documents, eMRTDs）的技术实现、验证过程、实际应用中的问题以及潜在的安全隐患。

不同观点：
• [tauntz] 指出ICAO 9303规范详细描述了如何读取和验证旅行证件数据，但实际应用中存在很多对规范的“创造性解释”以及实现上的漏洞，导致软件开发者在处理不同国家颁发的证件时会遇到许多调试问题。
• [nemoniac] 分享了一段Python代码用于生成MRZ（机器可读区），并提到其荷兰驾照上的MRZ样式的编码部分难以解读，寻求帮助。
• [alexrsagen] 提供了Rust代码示例，说明如何读取护照照片和处理eMRTD，并表示对ICAO 9303规范的细节很感兴趣，认为其非常详细。
• [privacyking] 提出使用Proxmark 3 rdv4设备可以轻松读取MRZ数据，暗示这是获取此类信息的简便方法。
• [wkat4242] 提到护照中还包含数字化的指纹信息，但这些信息更难获取，因为需要政府持有的私钥才能解锁。
• [stavros] 质疑是否有遗漏关于如何处理缺失校验和的信息，尤其是是否能轻易通过已有信息计算校验和，或者是否有人成功解密护照。
• [extraduder_ire] 推荐了一款安卓应用，可以在没有NFC读取器的情况下读取护照数据，但用户需要手动输入部分信息。
• [SXX] 提出疑问，规范中是否包含护照颁发机构的数字签名，否则各国如何验证护照的真伪。
• [ape4] 对日期格式不兼容Y2K表示惊讶，难以相信在2025年还会遇到这种问题。
• [frelp] 担心有人可能会制造出能够破坏护照读取系统的芯片，从而引发安全隐患。
• [criddell] 询问这些技术是否仅适用于Linux系统，或者是否也适用于Windows和macOS。
• [dzhiurgis] 质疑是否可以通过在假护照中植入自定义照片和元数据来欺骗系统，并对系统的安全性表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是实际应用中的技术实现与规范的偏差，以及由此带来的调试和验证困难。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于护照数据的访问和安全问题，包括如何防止伪造和未经授权的访问。
• 不同用户提供了多种工具和代码示例，展示了如何读取和处理MRZ数据，并分享了实际操作中的经验和建议。
• 安全性和隐私问题也是讨论的重点，包括对数字签名、校验和以及潜在安全漏洞的关注。

44374574.article_content:
For boring and totally not nefarious reasons, I want to read all the data contained in my passport's NFC chip using Linux. After a long and annoying search, I settled on
roeften's pypassport
.
I can now read all the passport information, including biometrics.
Background
The NFC chip in a passport is protected by a password. The password is printed on the inside of the physical passport. As well as needing to be physically close to the passport for NFC to work
0
, you also need to be able to see the password. The password is printed in the "Machine Readable Zone" (MRZ) - which is why some border guards will swipe your passport through a reader before scanning the chip; they need the password and don't want to type it in.
I had a small problem though.  I'm using my old passport
1
which
has been cancelled
.  Cancelling isn't just about revoking the document. It is also physically altered:
Cut off the bottom left hand corner of the personal details page, making sure you cut the MRZ on the corner opposite the photo.
So a chunk of the MRZ is missing! Oh no! Whatever can we do!?
Recreating the MRZ
The password is made up of three pieces of data:
Passport Number (Letters and Numbers)
Date of Birth (YYMMDD)
Expiry Date (YYMMDD)
Each piece
also
has a checksum. This calculation is defined in Appendix A to
Part 3 of Document 9303
.
Oh, and there's a checksum for the entire string. It's this final checksum which is cut off when the passport cover is snipped.
The final password is:
Number Number-checksum DOB DOB-checksum Expiry Expiry-checkum checksum-of-previous-digits
Python code to generate an MRZ
If you know the passport number, date of birth, and expiry date, you can generate your own Machine Readable Zone - this acts as the password for the NFC chip.

Can you read a cancelled passport?
I would have thought that cutting the cover of the passport would destroy the antenna inside it. But, going back to
the UK guidance
:
You must not cut the back cover on the ePassport
Ah! That's where the NFC chip is. I presume this is so that cancelled passports can still be verified for authenticity.
Cryptography and other security
The security is, thankfully, all fairly standard Public Key Cryptography -
9303 part 11
explains it in
excruciating
levels of detail.
One thing I found curious - because the chip has no timer, it cannot know how often it is being read. You could bombard it with thousands of password attempts and not get locked out.  Indeed, the specification says:
the success probability of the attacker is given by the time the attacker has access to the IC, the duration of a single attempt to guess the password, and the entropy of the passport.
Can you brute-force a passport?
Wellllll… maybeeeee…?
Passports are generally valid for only 10 years. So that's 36,525 possible expiry dates.
Passport holders are generally under 100 years old. So that's 3,652,500 possible dates of birth.
That's already 133,407,562,500 attempts - and we haven't even got on to the 1E24 possible passport numbers!
In my experiments, sending an incorrect but valid MRZ results in the chip returning "Security status not satisfied (0x6982)" in a very short space of time. Usually less than a second.
But sending that incorrect attempt seemed to introduce a delay in the next response - by a few seconds. Sending the correct MRZ seemed to reset this and let the chip be read instantly.
So, if you knew the target's passport number and birthday, brute forcing the expiry date would take a couple of days. Not instant, but not impossible.
Most
commercial NFC chips support 100,000 writes
with no limit for the number of reads. Some also have a 24 bit read counter which increments after every read attempt. After 16 million reads, the counter doesn't increment. It
could
be possible for a chip to self-destruct aft

data.title: Bill Atkinson: Polaroids Showing the Evolution of the Lisa GUI [video]
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 该页面提供了多个链接，涵盖关于平台的信息、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者资源、广告、开发者信息以及使用条款等。同时包含隐私政策、安全指南以及YouTube的功能测试和新特性。此外，页面提及NFL Sunday Ticket和Google LLC的版权信息（© 2025）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bill Atkinson及其在软件开发和用户体验（UX）设计方面的贡献

不同观点：
• fidotron认为现代软件开发管理过于细分，难以出现像Bill Atkinson这样能够跨领域（从低级编程到UX设计）的全才。现代管理观念认为这样的人才是不可能存在的。
• oersted赞赏计算机历史博物馆，尤其是其由退休的业内资深志愿者运营，这些人有着丰富的经验和故事，使博物馆更加特别。
• mprovost强调了Bill Atkinson在“Atkinson dithering”算法方面的贡献，并提供了维基百科链接以供进一步了解。
• JKCalhoun对拖放操作（drag and drop）在开发中出现较晚表示惊讶，特别是在Finder试图解决用户发起的文件复制操作时才引入。
• smallduck指出Apple并非简单地复制Xerox Parc的概念，而是有其独特的创新。
• nxobject对视频中展示的内容进行了技术分析，认为这些内容是通过Apple II驱动Lisa的帧缓冲区至CRT子系统生成的。
• musicale赞赏Bill Atkinson的视频，并提到这些视频是对Andy Hertzfeld描述的补充，同时推荐了关于Lisa源代码的视频。
• HarHarVeryFunny回忆了在1980年伦敦的一个计算机展会上看到Lisa的演示，指出其当时价格昂贵且速度较慢。
• DonHopkins提供了多个链接，包括Bill Atkinson的采访、关于HyperCard的灵感来源（涉及LSD使用）以及PhotoCard应用的详细信息，强调了Bill Atkinson在多个领域的才华和贡献。
• vaxman对帖子的发布表示感谢，并对Bill Atkinson的去世表示哀悼。

补充讨论：
• 对Bill Atkinson的广泛影响和贡献进行了多方面的讨论，包括技术成就（QuickDraw、Atkinson dithering）、用户体验设计（拖放操作、用户测试）、以及他在其他领域（如HyperCard和PhotoCard）的创新。
• 讨论中涉及到对现代软件开发管理的批评，认为现代管理模式限制了跨领域人才的出现。
• 对计算机历史博物馆的赞赏，特别是其由退休行业资深志愿者运营的特点，增添了博物馆的历史和人文价值。
• 提供了多个外部链接以供进一步阅读和观看，丰富了讨论内容。
• 对Lisa的历史轶事及其在早期演示中的表现进行了个人回忆和评价。

data.title: Getting ready to issue IP address certificates
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IP地址证书的实用性、技术可行性、潜在风险及应用场景

不同观点：
• **支持S/MIME证书的观点**：  
  - [Tepix] 认为，虽然IP证书有用，但Let's Encrypt支持S/MIME证书会对电子邮件加密产生更大影响。当前，邮件客户端支持S/MIME，但需要可信CA颁发的证书，而免费且可信的长期S/MIME证书已经消失，导致私人用户不使用邮件加密。
  - 论据：邮件加密需要长期有效的证书来解密旧邮件，频繁更换不实际。

• **对IP证书技术的质疑**：  
  - [lq9AJ8yrfs] 提出IP地址频繁变动的问题，特别是在ISP和云服务商的情况下，质疑如何处理IP证书的循环使用和旧证书的撤销。
  - 论据：IP地址的快速轮换可能导致证书管理的复杂性，用户需要承担验证责任。

• **关于证书颁发机构的质疑**：  
  - [1vuio0pswjnm7] 质疑为什么地区互联网注册机构（RIR）和本地互联网注册机构（LIR）不直接颁发证书，而需要第三方CA验证。
  - 论据：质疑是否有必要依赖第三方CA，以及域名注册商为何不承担此任务。

• **技术实现与使用场景的讨论**：  
  - [mocko] 质疑IP证书的实际用例，认为技术上可行，但不清楚实际应用场景。
  - [vkdelta] 询问是否能通过这种证书解决本地路由器的HTTPS自签名证书错误问题。
  - [sschueller] 讨论内部IPv4地址的证书问题，建议浏览器对内部IP范围进行特殊处理。
  - [smallnix] 询问该证书是否适用于IPv4和IPv6。
  - [zaik] 提出是否能在XMPP联邦中使用此类证书。

补充讨论：
• **安全风险与潜在滥用**：  
  - [0xbadcafebee] 担心此举可能成为TLS的新漏洞，认为可能被黑客用于生成非自己拥有的IP地址的证书。
  - [richm44] 提及历史上的CVE-2010-3170漏洞，暗示可能重现类似问题。

• **技术细节与实现方式**：  
  - [sgjohnson] 提到IP地址证书无法通过DNS挑战，但理解其原因。
  - [OptionOfT] 讨论证书无主体的情况下，是否因为证书是为IP申请，而其他DNS条目属于SAN（主题备用名称）。

• **政策与官方立场**：  
  - [Hizonner] 要求提供官方对此举措的合理解释。

争议焦点：
- 证书的实际需求和应用场景不明确，特别是对IP地址证书的实际用途存在不同看法。
- 对证书颁发和管理的可行性及安全性存在担忧，特别是IP地址变动频繁的情况下如何有效管理证书。
- 对安全风险的担忧，尤其是可能被滥用生成非自己拥有的IP证书。

data.title: MCP in LM Studio
data.author: yags
data.article_summary: LM Studio 0.3.17 引入了对 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的支持，允许用户将本地和远程MCP服务器连接到应用，并通过 `mcp.json` 文件或新的“Add to LM Studio”按钮添加MCP服务器。新版本增加了11种新语言支持，总数达到33种，并修复了多个漏洞，改进了UI，新增了'Solarized Dark'主题。用户可以通过应用内更新或官网下载升级。MCP服务器提供工具和资源访问，需谨慎安装不可信来源的服务器。应用会在模型调用工具时显示确认对话框，用户可以管理工具权限。MCP服务器配置文件 `mcp.json` 位于系统特定路径，建议使用应用内编辑器修改。新功能还包括聊天外观设置、显示生成统计、支持固定下载面板等。开发者可以创建“Add to LM Studio”按钮简化MCP服务器添加。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LM Studio和MCP（Machine Created Protocols）服务器的使用体验、功能优化、技术细节以及相关工具的对比和整合。

不同观点：
• [jmetrikat] 认为通过LM Studio和本地模型试用MCP服务器非常方便，并分享了一个添加"Add to LM Studio"按钮的实例链接，方便用户操作。
• [chisleu] 提到自己花费12,000美元购买了一台Mac Studio用于运行LM Studio，强调LM Studio的优势在于将本地LLM（大语言模型）普及化，即使是非专业用户也能轻松使用。他还介绍了一个名为Exo的项目，可以自动集群网络中的主机以提高吞吐量。
• [mkagenius] 分享了在M1/M2/M3 Mac上使用Apple Containers自动执行生成代码的经验，并提供了一个配置示例和相关工具CodeRunner的链接。
• [sixhobbits] 对MCP术语的使用感到困惑，特别是"MCP Host"的定义，认为其容易引起误解，因为其他人都称之为"MCP Client"。
• [politelemon] 指出LM Studio和MCP的初体验不够友好，文档需要更清晰的指导。他提到了一些使用过程中遇到的具体问题，比如模型选择和工具使用上的困惑。
• [smcleod] 强调LM Studio的使用条款对工作相关用途非常不友好，提醒用户小心使用。
• [minimaxir] 认为LM Studio是Apple Silicon Mac上运行本地LLM的最佳选择，尽管对MCP并不看好，但这种方法提供了一种免费实验的途径。
• [b0a04gl] 提到通过LM Studio和MCP可以将笔记本配置成一个混合网格节点，实现本地和远程推理集群的结合。
• [xyc] 表示对MCP的支持使其工具（recurse.chat）更加实用，尽管在工具调用能力上还有待提高。
• [visiondude] 分享了LM Studio在M3 Ultra 64gb硬件上运行27b模型的良好体验。
• [patates] 询问其他用户在LM Studio上使用的模型、任务和内存情况，并分享了自己的使用案例。
• [jtreminio] 提出了如何在本地网络上使用LM Studio的问题，希望能在不同设备间无缝切换使用。
• [bbno4] 询问是否存在使用OpenRouter/Claude并支持MCP的应用。
• [squanchingio] 希望MCP服务器能像LM Studio的OpenAI-like端点一样被公开暴露。

补充讨论：
• LM Studio的用户界面和初次使用体验存在改进空间，尤其是文档和模型下载过程的引导。
• MCP术语的使用引起了部分用户的困惑，建议统一命名以避免误解。
• 用户对LM Studio的性能和功能总体满意，特别是在本地运行LLM的能力上，但对其使用条款存在一定担忧。
• 一些用户分享了将LM Studio与其他工具和项目结合使用的具体技术细节和实例。

44379792.article_content:
← Back to Blog
MCP in LM Studio
By
LM Studio Team
•
2025-06-25
LM Studio 0.3.17 introduces
Model Context Protocol (MCP) support
, allowing you to connect your favorite MCP servers to the app and use them with local models.
LM Studio supports both local and remote MCP servers. You can add MCPs by editing the app's
mcp.json
file or via the new
"Add to LM Studio" Button
, when available.
Also new in this release:
Support for 11 new languages, thanks to our community localizers. LM Studio is now available in 33 languages.
Many bug fixes, as well as improvements to the UI, including a new theme: 'Solarized Dark'.
Upgrade via in-app update, or from
https://lmstudio.ai/download
.
Add MCP servers to LM Studio
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a set of interfaces for providing LLMs access to tools and other resources. It was originally introduced by Anthropic, and is developed
on Github
.
Terminology:
"MCP Server"
: program that provides tools and access to resources. For example Stripe, GitHub, or Notion make MCP
servers
.
"MCP Host"
: applications (like LM Studio or Claude Desktop) that can connect to MCP servers, and make their resources available to models.
Install new servers:
mcp.json
Switch to the "Program" tab in the right hand sidebar. Click
Install > Edit mcp.json
.
This will open the
mcp.json
file in the in-app editor. You can add MCP servers by editing this file.
Edit mcp.json using the in-app editor
LM Studio currently follows Cursor's
mcp.json
notation.
Example MCP to try: Hugging Face MCP Server
This MCP server provides access to functions like model and dataset search.
{
"mcpServers"
:
{
"hf-mcp-server"
:
{
"url"
:
"https://huggingface.co/mcp"
,
"headers"
:
{
"Authorization"
:
"Bearer <YOUR_HF_TOKEN>"
}
}
}
}
You will need to replace
<YOUR_HF_TOKEN>
with your actual Hugging Face token. Learn more
here
.
Be cautious
Never install MCPs from untrusted sources.
Heads Up
Some MCP servers can run arbitrary code, access your local files, and use your network connection. Always be cautious when installing and using MCP servers. If you don't trust the source, don't install it.
Tool call confirmations
When a model calls a tool, LM Studio will show a confirmation dialog to the user. This allows you to review the tool call arguments before executing it, including editing the arguments if needed.
Tool call confirmation dialog
You can choose to always allow a given tool, always deny it, or allow it only once.
If you choose to always allow a tool, LM Studio will not show the confirmation dialog for that tool in the future. You can manage this later in
App Settings > Tools & Integrations
.
MCP support: more technical details
When you save the
mcp.json
file, LM Studio will automatically load the MCP servers defined in it. We spawn a separate process for each MCP server.
For local MCP servers that rely on
npx
or
uvx
(or any other program on your machine), you need to ensure those tools are installed and available in your system's PATH.
mcp.json
lives in
~/.lmstudio/mcp.json
on macOS and Linux, and in
%USERPROFILE%/.lmstudio/mcp.json
on Windows. It's recommended to use the in-app editor to edit this file.
If you're running into bugs, please open an issue on our bug tracker:
https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues
.
Developers: Create a 'Add to LM Studio' Button
We're also introducing a one-click way to add MCP servers to LM Studio using a deeplink button.
Install link generator
Enter your MCP JSON entry to generate a deeplink for the
Add to LM Studio
button.
👇 This is a real interactive tool that you can use to create your own MCP install links. Try it!
No MCP Server Detected
Markdown
HTML
Click on the button to copy the
Markdown
to clipboard.
Example
Try to copy and paste the following into the link generator above.
{
"hf-mcp-server"
:
{
"url"
:
"https://huggingface.co/mcp"
,
"headers"
:
{
"Authorization"
:
"Bearer <YOUR_HF_TOKEN>"
}
}
}
You will need to replace
<YOUR_HF_TOKEN>
with your actual Hugging Face token. Learn more
here
.
One more thing...
Connecting MCP servers is easy. But what about creating your own tools and custom resources for your models? Stay tuned... 👾
0.3.17 - Full Release Notes
Build 10
Added a Chat Appearance setting to display message generation stats on last message only, in tooltips only, or on all applicable messages
Token count now includes system prompt & tool definitions
Show 'open in browser' button for LLM messages that have a URL in the content.
Be mindful: LLMs may generate untrusted URLs. Always verify links before clicking.
Build 9
Enable MCP by default
Cmd + Shift + E
on Mac or
Ctrl + Shift + E
on PC always opens the system prompt editor for the current chat
Build 8
When download panel is open in a new window, add an option to pin it on top of other windows (right click the body)
Adds the following languages, thanks to our community localizers!
Malayalam (ml)
@prasanthc41m
Thai (th)
@gnoparus
Bosnian (bs)
@0haris0
Bulgarian (bg)
@DenisZekiria
Hungarian (hu)
@Mekemo

data.title: Interstellar Flight: Perspectives and Patience
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary: 本文由保罗·吉尔斯特撰写，探讨了星际飞行和人类技术的速度极限。文章从爵士音乐家约翰·柯川的专辑《Sun Ship》谈起，联想到帕克太阳探测器这一“太阳船”在2021年接近太阳的创举。作者反思了人类目前最快的速度记录，如阿波罗10号和帕克探测器的191.2公里/秒，指出即使以这种速度到达比邻星仍需约6600年。文章还提到旅行者1号将在2027年达到一光日的距离，并回顾了 Voyager 项目的工作量。作者通过这些数据，引发对星际飞行梦想和所需耐心的思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：星际旅行的可行性及其相关技术和哲学问题

不同观点：
• **星际旅行的现实困难**：imoreno认为即使距离我们仅4光年的半人马座阿尔法星，星际旅行也非常不现实。即使达到0.01c的速度，旅行时间也会长达几百年甚至上千年，且需要巨大的技术突破。语言变化和国家兴衰等社会问题也会影响这种旅行的可行性。此外，这种项目需要巨大的投资，但没有保证能见到成果。

• **意识上传与数字化永生**：Oleksa_dr提出，通过意识上传和数字化永生，人类可以克服时间对星际旅行的限制。这种方法可以通过将意识转移到机器中实现，而飞船则需要具备长时间自主运行的能力。

• **推进技术和太阳系扩张**：d_silin认为，开发达到0.1c速度的推进技术可以将星际旅行从不可能变为勉强可行，但至少需要100-200年。在此之前，我们可以先扩展到月球和火星等太阳系天体。

• **流浪行星和探索机会**：kfuse提出，银河系中可能存在大量流浪行星，这些行星可能比恒星周围的行星更易探索。Roman望远镜可能会在2027年帮助发现这些行星。

• **太阳系的实际探索**：southernplaces7认为，虽然星际旅行是一个有趣的梦想，但在现实中不可行。相比之下，太阳系内的探索和开发更为实际和现实，且资源丰富，足以支持人类千年以上的发展。

• **可持续性和环境问题**：krunck引用Benjamin Stockton的评论，质疑人类是否应更关注文明的可持续性和地球环境的保护，而不是冒险进行星际旅行。不过，krunck也承认太空飞行在行星防御和小行星采矿方面的必要性。

• **技术和社会问题**：lofaszvanitt对星际旅行的可行性持悲观态度，认为人类目前无法解决许多基本问题，如大规模森林火灾和天气控制，因此太空旅行的幻想是不切实际的。

• **光帆和粒子撞击问题**：os2warpman提到，利用光帆技术可以缩短到比邻星的旅行时间到20年，但飞船在高速下撞击尘埃粒子的风险极高，可能导致严重损坏。

• **机器后代作为旅行者**：xpuente认为，未来星际旅行的实现者可能是我们的机器后代，而不是人类自身。

• **纳米技术和星系生命传播**：WalterBright提出，通过发送小型航天器和纳米机器人，可以探索和传播地球生命，但这种方式依赖于从当地材料中建造必要设施。

• **戴森群和星际飞船**：jmyeet解释了戴森群作为人类文明进化的必然性，并提出利用太阳帆加速到0.01c的星际旅行方案。这种方法需要大量能量，可能通过戴森群收集。

• **梦想与现实**：agentultra认为，星际旅行的梦想可能只会停留在梦想阶段，因为距离太过遥远，且没有明确的目标或必要性。

• **技术限制和创新**：econ指出，要实现星际旅行，首先需要突破当前物理学对永动机和无反应驱动的限制，而这在目前看来是不可能的。

• **反物质火箭和星际旅行**：GMoromisato通过与ChatGPT的讨论得出结论，反物质火箭可能是唯一能够实现自给自足的星际飞船方案，其他技术如离子推进和核裂变都无法达到必要的速度。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于星际旅行的技术可行性和实际必要性。一些人认为星际旅行是遥不可及的梦想，而另一些人则认为通过技术进步和创新可以实现。此外，关于数字化永生和意识上传的讨论也提出了另一种星际探索的可能性。

Interstellar Flight: Perspectives and Patience
by
Paul Gilster
|
Jun 25, 2025
|
Culture and Society
|
1 comment
This morning’s post grows out of listening to John Coltrane’s album
Sun Ship
earlier in the week. If you’re new to jazz,
Sun Ship
is not where you want to begin, as Coltrane was already veering in a deeply avant garde direction when he recorded it in 1965. But over the years it has held a fascination for me. Critic Edward Mendelowitz called it “a riveting glimpse of a band traveling at warp speed, alternating shards of chaos and beauty, the white heat of virtuoso musicians in the final moments of an almost preternatural communion…” McCoy Tyner’s piano is reason enough to listen.
As music often does for me,
Sun Ship
inspired a dream that mixed the music of the Coltrane classic quartet (Tyner, Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones) with an ongoing story. The Parker Solar Probe is, after all, a real ‘sun ship,’ one that on December 24 of last year made its closest approach to the Sun. Moving inside our star’s corona is a first – the craft closed to within 6.1 million kilometers of the solar surface.
When we think of human technology in these hellish conditions, those of us with an interstellar bent naturally start musing about ‘sundiver’ trajectories, using a solar slingshot to accelerate an outbound spacecraft, perhaps with a propulsive burn at perihelion. The latter option makes this an ‘Oberth maneuver’ and gives you a maximum outbound kick. Coltrane might have found that intriguing – one of his later albums was, after all, titled
Interstellar Space
.
I find myself musing on speed. The fastest humans have ever moved is the 39,897 kilometers per hour that the trio of Apollo 10 astronauts – Tom Stafford, John Young and Eugene Cernan – experienced on their return to Earth in 1969. The figure translates into just over 11 kilometers per second, which isn’t half bad. Consider that Voyager 1 moves at 17.1 km/sec, and it’s the fastest object we’ve yet been able to send into deep space.
True, New Horizons has the honor of being the fastest craft immediately after launch, moving at over 16 km/sec and thus eclipsing Voyager 1’s speed before the latter’s gravity assists. But New Horizons has since slowed as it climbs out of the Sun’s gravitational well, now making on the order of 14.1 km/sec, with no gravity assists ahead. Wonderfully, operations continue deep in the Kuiper Belt.
It’s worth remembering that at the beginning of the 20th Century, a man named Fred Mariott became the fastest man alive when he managed 200 kilometers per hour in a steam-powered car (and somehow survived). Until we launched the Parker Solar Probe, the two Helios missions counted as the fastest man-made objects, moving in elliptical orbits around the Sun that reached 70 kilometers per second. Parker outdoes this: At perihelion in late 2024, it managed 191.2 km/sec, so it now holds velocity as well as proximity records.
191.2 kilometers per second gets you to Proxima Centauri in something like 6,600 years. A bit long even for the best equipped generation ship, I think you’ll agree. Surely Heinlein’s ‘Vanguard,’ the starship in
Orphans of the Sky
was moving at a much faster clip even if its journey took many centuries to reach the same star. I don’t think Heinlein ever let us know just how many. Of course, we can’t translate the Parker spacecraft’s infalling velocity into comparable numbers on an outbound journey, but it’s fun to speculate on what these numbers imply.
Image:
The United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy rocket launches NASA’s Parker Solar Probe to touch the Sun, Sunday, Aug. 12, 2018, from Launch Complex 37 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida. Parker Solar Probe is humanity’s first-ever mission into a part of the Sun’s atmosphere called the corona. The mission continues to explore solar processes that are key to understanding and forecasting space weather events that can impact life on Earth. It also gives a nudge to interstellar dreamers. Credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls.
Speaking of Voyager 1, another interesting tidbit relates to distance: In 2027, the perhaps still functioning spacecraft will become the first human object to reach one light-day from the Sun. That’s just a few steps in terms of an interstellar journey, but nonetheless meaningful. Currently radio signals take over 23 hours to reach the craft, with another 23 required for a response to be recorded on Earth. Notice that 2027 will also mark the 50th year since the two Voyagers were launched. January 28, 2027 is a day to mark in your calendar.
Since we’re still talking about speeds that result in interstellar journeys in the thousands of years, it’s also worth pointing out that 11,000 work-years were devoted to the Voyager project through the Neptune encounter in 1989, according to NASA. That is roughly the equivalent of a third of the effort estimated to complete the Great Pyramid at Giza during the reign of Khufu, (~2580–2560 BCE) in the fourth dynasty of the O

data.title: Iroh: A library to establish direct connection between peers
data.author: gasull
data.article_summary: Iroh 是一个基于公钥拨号的 API，能够自动寻找并维持最快网络连接，支持打洞技术以实现直接连接，失败时可回退到公共中继服务器。它使用 QUIC 协议，提供认证加密、并发流、数据报传输等功能，避免线头阻塞。Iroh 提供了多个预定义协议，如 iroh-blobs 用于内容寻址的大规模数据传输，iroh-gossip 用于建立发布-订阅网络。此外，Iroh 还支持 Rust 以外的其他语言通过 FFI 绑定使用。项目包含多个子模块，如核心库 iroh、中继服务器实现 iroh-relay 等，并采用 Apache-2.0 和 MIT 双重许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Iroh的功能、实现及其与其他P2P工具的比较

不同观点：
• Ingon：Ingon从connet的角度分析了Iroh的设计。他认为Iroh的relay和discovery合并为一个服务，而connet是分开的。此外，Iroh使用TCP而connet使用QUIC，可能会有head-of-line blocking问题。Ingon还指出Iroh的ALPN协议选择机制比connet的"虚拟连接"协议更灵活，且Iroh的命名和角色分配更复杂。
• eminence32：认为Iroh从最初计划取代IPFS的宏大目标，转变为专注于成为高质量的P2P应用库，是明智的选择。他赞赏Iroh不再试图成为万能工具，而是专注于核心功能。
• aquariusDue：分享了参加Iroh工作坊的经历，提到Iroh即将发布1.0版本，并介绍了基于Iroh的应用Dumb Pipe和SendMe。他还提到Iroh使用Bittorrent DHT Mainline进行发现，且客户端需要在同一relay上。
• conradev：对Iroh的YouTube解释视频表示赞赏，并期待FFI的实现。
• ndyg：对Iroh和Dumbpipe表示兴趣，认为其易于理解和使用。
• bestouff：指出Iroh用Rust编写，但在嵌入式系统中使用存在问题，如缺乏no_std版本和CAN插件。
• Python3267：询问Iroh与libP2P的比较。
• b0a04gl：从模块化嵌入式工具的角度，询问是否可以在保持Bittorrent DHT发现逻辑的同时，替换传输层为gRPC。
• throw10920：希望有类似Syncthing的发现机制，但认为Iroh使用的低级语言是个障碍。
• splintercell：正在使用GunDB，询问从GunDB迁移到Iroh需要什么。
• swoorup：询问Iroh是否仅限于P2P架构，还是也支持客户端-服务器架构。

补充讨论：
• 关于Iroh与libp2p的比较是另一个讨论焦点，部分参与者（如Python3267和outside1234）认为需要更详细的对比分析。outside1234还提到libp2p可能是一个更低级的工具包，需要自行组装。
• Iroh的应用场景和潜力被多次提及，尤其是aquariusDue对Iroh在视频游戏流媒体中的应用和ndyg的日常使用经验。
• 技术实现上的细节如协议选择、传输层实现、嵌入式系统兼容性等问题也被多位讨论者关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在Iroh与libp2p的比较以及技术实现上的取舍，如TCP与QUIC的选择及其潜在问题。

What is iroh?
Iroh gives you an API for dialing by public key.
You say “connect to that phone”, iroh will find & maintain the fastest connection for you, regardless of where it is.
Hole-punching
The fastest route is a direct connection, so if necessary, iroh tries to hole-punch.
Should this fail, it can fall back to an open ecosystem of public relay servers.
To ensure these connections are as fast as possible, we
continuously measure iroh
.
Built on
QUIC
Iroh uses
Quinn
to establish
QUIC
connections between nodes.
This way you get authenticated encryption, concurrent streams with stream priorities, a datagram transport and avoid head-of-line-blocking out of the box.
Compose Protocols
Use pre-existing protocols built on iroh instead of writing your own:
iroh-blobs
for
BLAKE3
-based content-addressed blob transfer scaling from kilobytes to terabytes
iroh-gossip
for establishing publish-subscribe overlay networks that scale, requiring only resources that your average phone can handle
iroh-docs
for an eventually-consistent key-value store of
iroh-blobs
blobs
iroh-willow
for an (in-construction) implementation of the
willow protocol

44379173.article_summary: Iroh 是一个基于公钥拨号的 API，能够自动寻找并维持最快网络连接，支持打洞技术以实现直接连接，失败时可回退到公共中继服务器。它使用 QUIC 协议，提供认证加密、并发流、数据报传输等功能，避免线头阻塞。Iroh 提供了多个预定义协议，如 iroh-blobs 用于内容寻址的大规模数据传输，iroh-gossip 用于建立发布-订阅网络。此外，Iroh 还支持 Rust 以外的其他语言通过 FFI 绑定使用。项目包含多个子模块，如核心库 iroh、中继服务器实现 iroh-relay 等，并采用 Apache-2.0 和 MIT 双重许可。
44379173.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Iroh的功能、实现及其与其他P2P工具的比较

不同观点：
• Ingon：Ingon从connet的角度分析了Iroh的设计。他认为Iroh的relay和discovery合并为一个服务，而connet是分开的。此外，Iroh使用TCP而connet使用QUIC，可能会有head-of-line blocking问题。Ingon还指出Iroh的ALPN协议选择机制比connet的"虚拟连接"协议更灵活，且Iroh的命名和角色分配更复杂。
• eminence32：认为Iroh从最初计划取代IPFS的宏大目标，转变为专注于成为高质量的P2P应用库，是明智的选择。他赞赏Iroh不再试图成为万能工具，而是专注于核心功能。
• aquariusDue：分享了参加Iroh工作坊的经历，提到Iroh即将发布1.0版本，并介绍了基于Iroh的应用Dumb Pipe和SendMe。他还提到Iroh使用Bittorrent DHT Mainline进行发现，且客户端需要在同一relay上。
• conradev：对Iroh的YouTube解释视频表示赞赏，并期待FFI的实现。
• ndyg：对Iroh和Dumbpipe表示兴趣，认为其易于理解和使用。
• bestouff：指出Iroh用Rust编写，但在嵌入式系统中使用存在问题，如缺乏no_std版本和CAN插件。
• Python3267：询问Iroh与libP2P的比较。
• b0a04gl：从模块化嵌入式工具的角度，询问是否可以在保持Bittorrent DHT发现逻辑的同时，替换传输层为gRPC。
• throw10920：希望有类似Syncthing的发现机制，但认为Iroh使用的低级语言是个障碍。
• splintercell：正在使用GunDB，询问从GunDB迁移到Iroh需要什么。
• swoorup：询问Iroh是否仅限于P2P架构，还是也支持客户端-服务器架构。

补充讨论：
• 关于Iroh与libp2p的比较是另一个讨论焦点，部分参与者（如Python3267和outside1234）认为需要更详细的对比分析。outside1234还提到libp2p可能是一个更低级的工具包，需要自行组装。
• Iroh的应用场景和潜力被多次提及，尤其是aquariusDue对Iroh在视频游戏流媒体中的应用和ndyg的日常使用经验。
• 技术实现上的细节如协议选择、传输层实现、嵌入式系统兼容性等问题也被多位讨论者关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在Iroh与libp2p的比较以及技术实现上的取舍，如TCP与QUIC的选择及其潜在问题。

不同观点：

• gaudat建议使用Synology NAS和其Photos应用来备份iPhone和Android设备的Live Photos，并认为NAS对大多数用户是可行的。

• jlarocco认为ifuse和rsync足以满足个人需求，但理解其对家庭成员可能有用。
• atmosx分享了自己通过PhotoSync将iPhone照片备份到自建的Photoprism服务的经验，使用WebDAV并通过tailscale进行远程访问。
• polymatter对“终身”支付选项表示赞赏。
• SwamyM希望有一种方法能方便地仅备份自己拍摄的照片，而非所有来源的图片。
• 1970-01-01提问这种备份方法与iMazing有何不同。
• mindwork询问Immich是否适合这种备份需求，并指出可在Docker容器中运行。
• mfa1999关注备份大型照片库（如150k照片/视频）的可行性，以及是否保留相册/文件夹结构。
• keroro询问相关工具的成本。
• er0k简单表示自己使用rsync，效果很好。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于NAS方案是否适合大多数用户，gaudat认为可行，而其他用户未明确回应这一观点。

• 备份大型照片库的具体需求和实现方式引起了关注，特别是对数据量大和复杂结构的处理能力。
• 成本问题也被提及，尤其是对终身支付选项的偏好。

data.title: The Offline Club
data.author: esher
data.article_summary: 《The Offline Club》倡导远离屏幕、享受线下生活。他们举办各种数字戒毒静修、商务活动和线下聚会，帮助人们放松、交流和建立真实联系。俱乐部已在多个城市设立分会，如阿姆斯特丹、伦敦、巴黎等，并计划扩展到更多地方。参与者可以通过加入当地等待名单或申请成为城市领袖来启动新分会。俱乐部还提供周末静修活动，让人远离日常繁忙和数字干扰。此外，他们发布《The Offline Times》新闻通讯，分享灵感与建议，并定期举办全球24小时数字戒毒挑战。用户评价极高，4.7分（基于251条评论）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对The Offline Club及类似社交活动的看法与挑战

不同观点：
• **apgwoz**：认为The Offline Club与Meetup类似，面临相同的挑战，如寻找活动场地、确保报名者实际参加、激励组织者持续举办活动等。但The Offline Club不围绕特定主题，而是强调“线下”互动，可能创造更多兴趣机会。
• **esher**：对The Offline Club无 affiliation，只是分享发现。个人对参加柏林的活动有兴趣，但因地点是“ hipster区”而犹豫。
• **larrymyers**：认为类似The Offline Club的场所已经存在，如本地游戏店，这些地方天然禁止设备使用，强制离线互动。
• **lfxyz**：曾参加阿姆斯特丹的活动，需上交手机，花了10欧元，觉得体验不错但价格高， unlikely to成为常规活动。
• **kilroy123**：指出The Offline Club嵌入了https://lu.ma/，认为有些讽刺。
• **JR1427**：通过加入本地帆船俱乐部改变了对俱乐部和社团的看法，推荐寻找类似俱乐部。
• **syhol**：原本期待是local-first软件倡导，有些失望，但承认自己可能需要更多线下体验。
• **aryehof**：建议创建一个非盈利俱乐部，提供安静的线下社交空间，有严格规则，如仅限会员、禁止电子设备等。
• **yesfitz**：认为The Offline Club有特定市场需求，尤其是对屏幕成瘾者，付费参加活动可以提供一种确定感和无技能要求的社交体验。
• **edent**：质疑花12.50英镑仅为安静阅读的性价比。
• **ethagnawl**：欢迎The Offline Club，认为其是无WeWork包袱的Meetup替代品，个人曾在Meetup上成功交友。
• **tonymet**：认为真正的社交生活应是 spontaneous的，过度安排和计划反而让社交变得无趣和脆弱。
• **PolyBaker**：幽默指出讨论在一个在线文章中进行。
• **quijoteuniv**：幽默期待网站不可用的笑话。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：The Offline Club是否值得付费参加，尤其是与免费替代方案（如咖啡店）相比。
- **核心讨论**：活动的市场需求、组织挑战、付费参与的合理性，以及线下社交的本质是 spontaneous还是计划性。

data.title: Writing a basic Linux device driver when you know nothing about Linux drivers
data.author: sbt567
data.article_summary: 文章主要描述了作者尝试为Nanoleaf Pegboard Desk Dock开发Linux驱动程序的过程。该设备原本只支持Windows和macOS系统，作者通过在Windows虚拟机中进行USB直通和逆向工程官方驱动，尝试了解设备协议。意外的是，Nanoleaf技术支持快速提供了详细的协议文档。作者利用这些信息，结合Linux系统中的`lsusb`工具，分析设备描述符和接口信息，发现Linux内核已为该设备分配了一个基础驱动，但功能有限。文章进一步介绍了USB设备的基本知识，并计划基于逆向工程的协议开发完整的Linux驱动。最终，作者提供了相关代码链接，并继续探索开发过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源技术文档、技术简化与复杂性、项目实现与期望、技术选择与学习曲线、生产环境中的应用、AI辅助编程的可能性

不同观点：
• [ahartmetz] 赞赏Nanoleaf主动分享技术协议文档，认为这与那些过度保护所谓"知识产权"的厂商形成对比。
• [rkagerer] 一方面赞赏当前技术进步，另一方面怀念过去简单的硬件接口，认为现代协议如USB过于复杂，丧失了早期技术探索的乐趣。
• [rajiv256] 分享了自己在Rust中编写以太网驱动程序的经历，并提供了项目链接，表现出对技术实践的热情。
• [ianlevesque] 指出文章中的项目是用户空间的USB HID驱动，而不是内核驱动，认为这更具实际应用性。
• [dabedee] 赞赏文章的写作方式，认为通过展示代码和错误路径让读者体验了作者的思考过程。
• [bhasi] 认为文章标题有误导性，因为实际项目不是Linux内核驱动。
• [blahgeek] 对文章未涉及AI编码表示惊喜，表现出对AI编码趋势的预期。
• [kblissett] 对用户空间驱动在生产环境中的具体应用提出疑问，关注其实际部署和配置方式。
• [LorenDB] 建议作者将项目整合到OpenRGB中，以更好地服务社区，表现出对开源贡献的期望。
• [0xbadcafebee] 提到希望在FreeBSD上运行但缺乏WiFi驱动，考虑使用AI编码助理但因学习成本而放弃。

A couple of months ago I bought the
Nanoleaf Pegboard Desk Dock
, the latest and greatest in USB-hub-with-RGB-LEDs-and-hooks-for-gadgets technology. This invention unfortunately only supports the
real gamer
operating systems of Windows and macOS, which necessitated the development of a Linux driver.
Over the past few posts Iâve set up a
Windows VM with USB passthrough
, and attempted to
reverse-engineer the official drivers
,  As I was doing that, I also thought Iâd message the vendor and ask them if they could share any specifications or docs regarding their protocol. To my surprise, Nanoleaf tech support responded to me within 4 hours, with a full description of the protocol thatâs used both by the Desk Dock as well as their RGB strips. The docs mostly confirmed what I had already discovered independently, but there were a couple of other minor features as well (like power and brightness management) that I did not know about, which was helpful.
Today, weâre going to take a crack at writing a driver based on the (reverse-engineered) protocol, while also keeping
the official documentation
at hand. One small problem, though: Iâve never written a Linux device driver before, nor interacted with any USB device as anything else but a user.
Skip to the good part?
Lots of yapping ahead. If you just want to see the code,
click here
.
Starting from scratch
Most Linux distros ship with
lsusb
, a simple utility that will enumerate all USB devices connected to the system. Since I had no clue where to start from, I figured I might as well run this to see if the device appears in the listing.
$ lsusb
<snip>
Bus 001 Device 062: ID 37fa:8201 JW25021301515 Nanoleaf Pegboard Desk Dock
Well, good news, itâs definitely there. But, how can the kernel know that what I have plugged in is the âNanoleaf Pegboard Desk Dockâ? The kernel (presumably) has no knowledge of this deviceâs existence, yet the second I plug it in to my computer it receives power, turns on and gets identified by the kernel.
As it turns out, we actually already have a driver! Itâs just a very stupid one. If we run
lsusb
in verbose mode and request the information just for this specific device, we will get a lot more details about it:

A quick USB class

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）中的“幻觉”问题及其影响和解决方案

不同观点：
• simonw：认为生成代码中的幻觉问题并不严重，因为错误在运行时会立即显现，而且LLM本身在尝试运行代码时能够发现错误。他还对论文中更多讨论RAG（检索增强生成）解决方案而非基于工具使用的解决方案表示惊讶，认为后者是更为成熟的解决方案。

• tmaly：通过试验和错误得出类似结论，提供一次性代码示例作为上下文能获得最好的结果。

• rbanffy：指出当我们说LLM“幻觉”时，其实和人类犯错类似，只是人类犯错被称为“错误”。

• imiric：认为需要更多研究来解决幻觉这一根本问题，但AI公司更关注追逐基准和推出增值产品。RAG解决方案虽然有趣但有限，因为需要用户提供真实数据，而这对于大多数其他事实信息来说更加困难。依赖网络数据需要人工审查，因此并不是一个普遍适用的解决方案。

• dzikibaz：质疑LLM幻觉与低质量训练数据集或过度随机采样设置导致的随机标记有何不同。

• nerdjon：提到在生成IAM策略时，键常常基于预期被幻觉化，导致错误或不存在的高级条件。

• th0ma5：认为文章很好地讨论了在没有真实信息的情况下面对的许多问题，并对人们开发的各种解决方法表示兴趣。

• dheera：觉得LLM幻觉出一个不存在的Python库很可爱，因为这可能意味着它值得被创造出来。

• cryptica：怀疑LLM幻觉是由于训练集中的矛盾导致的，类似于人类在学习时不仔细处理知识矛盾会导致错误。提出了一种防止矛盾信息更新到模型的复杂训练方法。

补充讨论：
• simonw和imiric之间存在对RAG解决方案有效性的不同看法。simonw认为基于工具使用的解决方案更成熟，而imiric认为RAG解决方案有限且需要更根本的解决方案。

• cryptica提出了一个复杂的技术方案，通过检测训练中的矛盾信息来防止幻觉，这与其他评论者关注实际应用中的问题形成对比。

• 整体讨论显示出对幻觉问题的多角度理解，包括实际应用中的影响、技术解决方案以及对AI行业趋势的批评。

data.title: Microsoft Dependency Has Risks
data.author: ArcHound
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了微软依据美国制裁政策封锁国际刑事法院（ICC）一名官员邮箱的事件，引发了对依赖微软产品的组织可能面临风险的担忧。作者分析了此类事件再次发生的可能性及其潜在成本，提出企业应投资于预防措施。文章提到，尽管部分消息来源证实了封锁事件，微软和ICC均未进一步说明细节。作者强调，在当前美国政治环境下，制裁具有不可预测性，企业需考虑这种风险对其业务连续性的影响。最后，文章建议通过“安全投资回报计算”来理性评估应对此类风险的成本和措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对微软及相关技术服务的评价与风险分析

不同观点：
• **bob1029**：认为不应全面抵制微软，因为其拥有如.NET、MSSQL、Visual Studio等独特且优秀的工具和服务，特别是在调试体验上无可替代。不过，Azure和Windows存在较多问题。
• **hilbert42**：对许多公司依赖微软的云服务（如Azure）表示担忧，认为这是单一故障点，风险极高，类似于使用谷歌或YouTube等不可替代的服务。
• **neepi**：指出问题不在于微软本身，而是将业务外包给不可替代的服务提供商的风险。只要技术具有可替代性，风险就会降低。
• **jimbobimbo**：认为不应单独针对微软，因为所有美国公司都可能面临美国政府的要求，谷歌、亚马逊、苹果等也一样。
• **ArcHound**：作为作者澄清主要观点，指出从财务角度看，放弃微软并不理智，因为大多数企业依赖微软的服务（如AD、Teams、Outlook）。
• **graemep**：对成本论点持怀疑态度，认为大多数企业无需在微软的规模下运营，且微软的效率未必高，因此不应默认微软是最佳选择。
• **firesteelrain**：认为对于大多数企业来说，放弃微软的成本和困难远超过其带来的好处。

补充讨论：
• **throwaway48476**：指出在全球化逆转的背景下，企业需要考虑所在国的法律风险，并将这些风险纳入考量。
• **zombot**：提到特朗普时期政治的不确定性，使得与美国公司保持联系充满风险，特别是对于美国以外的公司。
• **xvilka**：提到GitHub也带来类似风险，建议建立去中心化的开源替代方案，如GitLab Federation或Forgejo。
• **1970-01-01**：认为好的业务连续性计划应包括对任何风险的接受，并通过保险等补偿控制来缓解风险。
• **0xWTF**：提到当前社会对技术的依赖使得理解和掌控技术变得困难，个人运行自己的服务器等变得不切实际，因此不得不依赖现有的大型服务商。
• **hooverd**：引用一个近期事件，指出微软可能封锁受制裁个人的邮箱，提醒高度依赖微软产品的组织应考虑类似风险，并进行预防投资。
• **AndyMcConachie**：简单指出公司存在于司法管辖区内，必须遵循当地法律，暗示这是所有公司共同面临的问题。

争议焦点：
• 是否应全面抵制微软，特别是其云服务，如Azure。
• 微软是否在某些技术领域无可替代。
• 是否应将业务外包给可能存在单一故障点的服务提供商。
• 在当前全球化和法律环境下，如何有效管理与美国公司合作的风险。

There was a recent incident where
Microsoft somehow allegedly blocked a mailbox of a sanctioned individual
. Any organization highly depending on MS products that might come into the crosshair should ask - can this happen to me? What would be the cost? How much I invest into prevention of this scenario? In this article I try to get the facts straight and use a
return on security investment calculation
to try and judge this situation in a rational way. Let’s grab our tinfoil hats and find out if it’ll be fine.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
Orange screen of death exists, and seemed very fitting for this article.
I don’t like to cover recent news. But I do want to take a moment and consider a couple of implications of the recent alleged blocking of Microsoft services for the
ICC
.
For better or for worse, availability and business continuity usually fall under the security umbrella. That’s why I want to have a clear reference of this situation and some organized thoughts.
I will try and stick to the facts and hypotheticals. If you catch me having and voicing an opinion, please let me know and I’ll try and adjust accordingly. Alternatively, feel free to take a drink whenever you spot an opinion and then blame your drunkness on this article. For legal reasons that’s a joke.
I have these questions:
What happened?
What is the probability of an MS cutoff?
What is the cost of an MS cutoff?
How much should I invest to prevent this?
I’ll try to answer each of those in a separate section.
Microsoft blocked ICC employee mailbox?
The story summarized for a tweet is basically: Trump introduced sanctions against ICC and Microsoft disabled an account of at least one of such officials, locking them out of their work mailbox.
Sources supporting the claim:
Trump’s sanctions on ICC prosecutor have halted tribunal’s work
(Associated Press, 15-05-2025)
Microsoft's ICC email block triggers Dutch concerns over dependence on U.S. tech
(NL Times, 20-05-2025)
Sources disputing the claim:
Microsoft didn’t cut services to International Criminal Court, its president says
(Politico, 04-06-2025)
Here there’s a claim that only a single person was targeted, rather than the whole court. But they don’t dispute the single person target in the article.
Critical part:
Microsoft declined to comment further in response to questions regarding the exact process that led to Khan's email disconnection, and exactly what it meant by “disconnection.” The ICC declined to comment.
Other sources:
Microsofts Lösung für das Trump-Problem
(Wirtschafts Woche, 05-06-2025)
Danish department determined to dump Microsoft
(The Register, 13-06-2025)
There is a non-zero chance of this event repeating
The chain of events observed is roughly:
USA imposes sanctions
Microsoft complies with said sanctions by blocking their customer.
I am not a lawyer, so I won’t go into any detail of whether this is legal. I’d rather argue that by the time legality is established, the damage has already been done. No doubt that plenty of requests will be perfectly legal.
No reason required to impose sanctions
I have to talk about the current US president, since it seems that he has massive power over this process.
The Trump politics are, for a lack of a better publishable word, unpredictable. This is even worse than if he was straight up hostile to everyone, because then it would be easier to justify a very costly change. Check
this
for further explanation, especially:
Ironically, Trump’s additional goal of “reshoring” manufacturing to the U.S. is undercut by his own tariff unpredictability. Both domestic and foreign investors are loath to invest in reshored or new U.S. industries when there is no way to know what the specific tariffs will be for each product and each country.
There seems to be no clear way of knowing whether you or your company will be at odds with Trump (and, by extension, with USA) in near future.
Ok, so a decision to impose sanctions was made. Can it be executed?
It seems so that yes
.
Surely, this is temporary - after all, it’s his second term and that will end one day. Or not -
Trump Says He Will ‘Negotiate’ Third Term Because He’s ‘Entitled’ To It
. That will be decided in 2028, which is sort of far away

data.title: Libxml2's "no security embargoes" policy
data.author: jwilk
data.article_summary:
Libxml2是一个广泛使用的开源XML解析工具包，自2000年发布以来，被众多开源项目、商业软件和政府采用。然而，尽管许多组织乐于使用开源软件，却很少有人愿意为其持续维护做出贡献。这导致libxml2的当前维护者拒绝接受安全禁运（security embargoes）政策，引发了对自由和开源软件项目维护条款的讨论。

Libxml2由Daniel Veillard为GNOME项目开发，后在2000年代初被广泛采用，支持多种编程语言和操作系统。随着时间推移，Veillard的维护工作逐渐减少，Nick Wellnhofer在2013年开始贡献代码并承担大部分发布工作。2021年，由于Veillard忙于工作，加之安全漏洞修复延迟，Wellnhofer一度暂停维护，但随后在谷歌捐赠下于2022年恢复，并计划通过Open Source Collective获得资助。

文章反映了开源项目在长期维护和资金支持方面的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目维护者面临的压力、安全漏洞的定义与处理、企业对开源项目的利用与回馈

不同观点：
• 一些评论者（如h43z、lukaslalinsky）认为，维护者面临的压力主要来自心理层面，尤其是被企业利用和剥削的感觉。他们认为维护者需要学会拒绝不合理的要求，特别是面对企业对时间和精力的过度需求。
• arp242和DeepYogurt指出，许多被标记为“安全漏洞”的问题实际上并不是真正的安全隐患，例如拒绝服务（DoS）问题，或者是一些理论上的代码问题。他们认为过度的安全报告和CVE（常见漏洞与暴露）分配让维护者疲于应付，且影响了真正严重问题的处理。
• kibwen和jonathanlydall提到，大公司利用开源项目但回馈甚少，这种行为类似于“公共资源的监管俘获”。他们建议维护者可以通过选择如GPL等更严格的许可证来防止企业滥用开源软件。
• djoldman和atemerev持更激进的立场，认为维护者没有义务回应用户的任何压力，因为开源项目本身就是一种慈善贡献。如果用户不满意，可以选择自行 fork 项目并进行维护。
• KingOfCoders建议开源项目应该明确声明其对安全修复、外部贡献的立场，并提倡建立一种标准化的“维护条款”，以便各方清楚了解预期。

• SAI_Peregrinus讨论了负责任披露的两种方式：协调披露和完全披露，认为维护者有权选择默认完全披露。
• bryanlarsen和JonChesterfield对libxml2等关键基础设施项目的现状表示担忧，认为这些项目不应只是个人爱好项目，而应获得更多支持。

Libxml2's "no security embargoes" policy
[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Joe Brockmeier
June 25, 2025
Libxml2
, an
XML parser and toolkit, is an almost perfect example of the successes
and failures of the open-source movement. In the 25 years since its
first release, it has been widely adopted by open-source projects, for
use in commercial software, and for government use. It also
illustrates that while many organizations love using open-source software,
far fewer have yet to see value in helping to sustain it. That has led
libxml2's current maintainer to reject security embargoes and sparked
a discussion about maintenance terms for free and open-source
projects.
A short libxml2 history
The original
libxml
,
also known as gnome-xml, was written by Daniel Veillard for the GNOME
project. He also developed its successor,
libxml2
,
which was released in early 2000 under the MIT license, even though
GNOME applications tended to be under the GPLv2.
In the early 2000s, Veillard seemed eager to have others adopt
libxml2 outside the GNOME project. It was originally hosted on its own
site rather than on GNOME infrastructure. Libxml2 is written in C, but
had
language
bindings
for C++, Java, Pascal, Perl, PHP, Python, Ruby, and
more. The landing page listed a slew of standards implemented by
libxml2, as well as the variety of operating systems that it
supported, and boasted that it "
passed all 1800+ tests from the
OASIS XML Tests Suite
". The "
reporting
bugs and getting help
" page gave extensive guidance on how to
report bugs, and also noted that Veillard would attend to bugs or
missing features "
in a timely fashion
". The page, captured by
the Internet Archive in 2004, makes no mention of handling security
reports differently than bug reports—but those were simpler
times.
One can see why organizations felt comfortable, and even encouraged, to
adopt libxml2 for their software. Why reinvent the extremely
complicated wheel when someone else has not only done it but also
bragged about their wheel's suitability for purpose and given it a
permissive license to boot?
By the late 2000s, the project had matured, and the pace of
releases slowed accordingly. Veillard continued to maintain the
project, but skimming through the
GNOME xml
mailing list
shows that his attention was largely elsewhere. Nick
Wellnhofer began to make regular contributions to the project around
2013, and by 2017 he was doing a great deal of work on the project,
eventually doing most of the work on releases—though Veillard
was still officially sending them out. He was also making similar
contributions to a related project,
libxslt
,
which is a processor for
Extensible Stylesheet
Language Transformations
(XSLT) which are used for transforming
XML documents into other XML documents or into HTML, plain text,
etc.
I want my libxml2
In April 2021, Stefan Behnel
complained
that it had been almost 18 months since the last libxml2
release. "
There have been a lot of fixes during that time, so, may
I kindly ask what's hindering a new release?
" Veillard
replied
that the reason was that he was too busy with work, and there was
"
something I would need to get in before a release
". That
something seems to be a security fix for
CVE-2021-3541
,
a flaw in libxml2 that could lead to a denial of service. The release
of libxml2
2.9.11
,
which fixed the CVE, and
2.9.12
,
seem to have been the last contributions from Veillard to the project.
Wellnhofer had become the de facto maintainer of libxml2 and
libxslt as Veillard was fading away from them, but he temporarily
stepped
down
in July 2021. He had been able to fund his work through
Chrome bug bounties and other Google programs, but: "
returns from
security research are diminishing quickly and I see no way to obtain a
minimal level of funding anymore
".
Veillard
thanked
Wellnhofer for his work, and said he was not sure that he would be
able to ensure the same level of care for the projects on his own:
"
that's obvious for anybody monitoring those lists lately
".
In January 2022, Wellnhofer
announced
that he was able to resume maintenance of libxml2 and libxslt through
2022, thanks to a donation from Google. He planned to move the
projects to GNOME's infrastructure and resume releases, plus set up an
official way to sponsor libxml2 development. Ultimately, he chose
Open Source
Collective
as a fiscal host. (LWN
covered
Open Source
Collective in 2024.) To date, it appears that the project has received the
immense sum of $11,00

data.title: Ambient Garden
data.author: fipar
data.article_summary: "ambient.garden: an algorithmic audio landscape" 是一个互动式音频体验网站。用户可以通过点击来探索不同的音景，拖动以环顾四周，并随时切换自动导航模式。网站加载完成后，用户可以沉浸在一个由算法生成的花园环境中，享受独特的音频体验。该平台旨在提供一种放松和探索的数字环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对AmbientGarden项目的各种功能、设计及其潜在改进的看法和建议

不同观点：
• 作者Pierre的观点：
  - 项目是开源的，包括生成音频的代码。
  - 所有音乐都是用纯律（just intonation）制作，最初是为了方便编程，但后来深入研究了和声。
  - 计划在下一版本中加入节奏元素，认为这将提升项目水平。

• Huhtenberg的观点：
  - 在Firefox浏览器上遇到问题，音频播放两秒后被切断，并出现权限错误。

• Darzu的观点：
  - 赞赏点阵渲染系统，尤其喜欢其对地形和植物的表现效果，希望看到更多类似场景，如森林和河流。

• Pugworthy的观点：
  - 建议加入生成声音的野生动物，如蝴蝶或鸟，以增加声音和图案的变化。

• Bravesoul2的观点：
  - 项目让人联想到teamLab，喜欢其生成性视觉和音乐的结合，期待在大屏幕上体验。

• ChipsRafferty的观点：
  - 建议树木也进行无限程序生成，创造探索体验。
  - 提出添加不同类型的动物，这些动物的移动会改变声音效果。

• Keyle的观点：
  - 推荐类似项目Generative.fm，可以同时播放，创造更丰富的体验。

• LeoPanthera的观点：
  - 项目让人想起Mike Oldfield的Tres Lunas和Maestro，这些作品在当时非常前卫。

• StephenPontes的观点：
  - 项目让他想起teamLab Planets的体验，尤其是“Flowers and People, Cannot Be Controlled but Live Together”部分，其音轨非常出色。

• Meindnoch的观点：
  - 对“水铃”（water bell）元素感到困惑，询问其作用。

• CuriouslyC的观点：
  - 想象有“个性”的角色生成环境音乐，根据偏好函数探索花园，产生情感驱动音乐。

• 5-的观点：
  - 项目让他想起Proteus游戏，喜欢其简约的互动性，询问是否有类似游戏。

• BenRutter的观点：
  - 赞赏项目的美好，认为互联网上仍有许多人为了乐趣创造精彩内容。

• Yreg的观点：
  - 喜欢静态天空的效果，认为无限树木的设想很酷。

• Zannabianca1997的观点：
  - 对巨大的“水铃”元素感到困惑，但也希望树木能无限延伸。

补充讨论：
- 用户对项目的视觉效果和声音设计表示赞赏，同时提出了多种增加互动性和探索性的建议，如加入动物、无限生成元素等。
- 一些用户分享了类似项目和作品，提供了参考和对比。
- 技术问题主要集中在音频播放权限上，表明在不同浏览器和平台上的兼容性需要改进。

data.author: wglb

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vera C. Rubin Observatory的首次图像及其数据处理、天文观测的潜力、技术与政治问题

不同观点：
• **数据处理与卫星干扰**：thomascountz提到对NRO（国家侦察局）卫星数据的清洗问题，引用了Scott Manley的视频，指出存档数据未被清洗，但警报管道被清洗。有人可能认为人造卫星数据已经被清洗，但NRO和国防部可能有自己的过滤机制。
• **标题准确性**：larrymcp认为标题应修正为"Earth's"而不是"Earths"，以符合语法并保持与原纽约时报标题的一致性。
• **天文观测的革命性**：SwtCyber对 cataloging 数十亿星系和每晚发现数百万变化感到兴奋，认为这是天文观测的新篇章。

补充讨论：
• **数据量与科学潜力**：keyle对每晚产生20TB数据表示惊讶，并期待这些高分辨率图像能够帮助解答许多未解之谜，尤其是否能在南半球找到答案。
• **星系与恒星的数量比较**：JKCalhoun对200亿个星系和170亿颗恒星的数字提出疑问，质疑是否可见星系比恒星多，当然这是在忽略星系由恒星组成的情况下。
• **政治与资金问题**：UltraSane提到该项目由国家科学基金会资助，但1800名NSF员工正被住房和城市发展部从办公室驱逐，引用了科学美国人上关于特朗普政府的文章。
• **政治与地域一致性**：mc32对数据处理设施位于加州、法国和英国表示质疑，认为政治分区不一致，可能暗示其他方面也不严谨。
• **对Starlink的不满**：PatronBernard对Starlink表达不满，虽然没有详细解释原因，但可能涉及Starlink卫星对天文观测的干扰问题。

争议焦点：
• **数据清洗的标准与责任**：对NRO和国防部是否拥有自己的数据过滤机制存在讨论。
• **政治因素对科学项目的影响**：包括NSF员工被驱逐可能对项目产生的影响以及数据处理设施的地域选择问题。

data.title: Better Auth, by a self-taught Ethiopian dev, raises $5M from Peak XV, YC
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Bereket Engida，一位来自埃塞俄比亚的自学成才的程序员，创建了开源认证工具Better Auth，旨在简化开发者管理用户认证的流程。该工具允许开发者直接在数据库中实现从简单到复杂的认证系统，避免将用户数据存储在第三方服务上，解决了现有工具如Auth0、Firebase等的局限性。Better Auth在发布后迅速获得了大量关注，周下载量超过15万次，GitHub星标数达1.5万，并拥有6000多人的社区。该项目最近获得了由Peak XV、Y Combinator等投资的500万美元种子资金。Better Auth目前免费使用，计划推出付费企业版，同时保持开源社区的特性。Engida在埃塞俄比亚独立开发了该工具，并在Y Combinator加速器中毕业。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Better Auth 作为 TypeScript 认证框架的优点、潜在问题以及商业模式

不同观点：
• **赞赏与支持**：
  - [chrisldgk] 认为 Better Auth 提供了强大的插件和集成能力，尤其是与 ORM（如 drizzle 和 prisma）的集成，使得认证逻辑易于管理，且具有良好的可扩展性。TypeScript 客户端也非常出色。

  - [haneul] 表示对 Better Auth 的新闻感到兴奋和赞赏。

• **商业模式的疑虑**：
  - [blackhaj7] 对 Better Auth 如何通过 VC 资金盈利表示关注，担心这会影响其质量。
  - [h1fra] 和 [arend321] 都提到对 Better Auth 商业模式的疑问，尤其是其作为非云服务的库如何盈利。

- Better Auth 的**商业模式**及其与现有成熟方案的**技术差异**是争议的核心。用户对其如何在市场中定位和盈利感到困惑，同时也担心其质量受 VC 资金影响。

44380185.article_content:
It’s rare to see a solo founder building a widely adopted developer infrastructure tool. Even more so if the founder happens to be from Africa.
Bereket Engida
, a self-taught programmer from Ethiopia, is quietly building what some developers say is the best authentication tool they’ve ever used.
Engida’s startup,
Better Auth
, offers an open source framework that promises to simplify how developers manage user authentication, and it’s caught the attention of some big name investors. It recently raised about $5 million in seed funding from Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India and Southeast Asia), Y Combinator, P1 Ventures, and Chapter One.
But the most interesting part here isn’t who’s on the startup’s cap table: Engida says he built the entire product back home in Ethiopia before he set foot in the U.S.
Engida told TechCrunch that he started programming at 18 after a friend declined to help him build an e-commerce search app, and he started working on the project himself. He went on to land some remote software jobs and eventually built a web analytics platform that lets developers monitor user behavior on their websites.
But throughout his various jobs, Engida says he kept seeing an issue popping up everywhere: authentication. Every app needs to manage how users sign in and out and reset passwords, and sometimes administrators need to handle permissions and user roles. But he found existing tools were either too limited or too rigid — companies like Auth0, Firebase, and NextAuth offer managed services, but they store user data externally, limit customization, and are expensive at scale.
“I remember needing an organization feature. It’s a very common use case for most SaaS applications, but it wasn’t available from these providers,” Engida told TechCrunch. “So I had to build it from scratch. It took me about two weeks, and I remember thinking, ‘This is crazy; there has to be a better way to solve this.’”
He then scrapped that project and began working on a TypeScript-based authentication framework that would let developers access user data via open source libraries, support common permissions use cases — like teams and roles — out of the box, and scale with plug-ins.

“The idea was that you could add advanced features in just two or three lines of code,” Engida said.
Why developers love it
Over six months working mostly from his bedroom in Ethiopia, Engida built the first version of the library that would go on to become Better Auth. When he posted it to GitHub in September 2024, developers quickly saw the potential.
Since then, Better Auth has clocked 150,000+ weekly downloads, 15,000+ GitHub stars, and a community of over 6,000 Discord members, the startup claims.
Better Auth’s pitch is simple: Let developers implement everything from simple authentication flows to enterprise-grade systems directly on their databases and embed it all on the back end. Unlike hosted services, Better Auth is an open source library that developers can integrate directly into their codebase, keeping all user data on premise, in their database. For companies wary of handing over critical user information to third parties, this feature alone is a major point.
The library has also found unexpected traction among early-stage AI startups, which need to build custom authentication flows that integrate with proprietary APIs, manage tokens securely, and be able to scale without racking up high costs.
“We first heard about the product from numerous startups we’ve worked with,” said Arnav Sahu, partner at Peak XV and former principal at Y Combinator. “Their auth product has seen phenomenal adoption among the next generation of AI startups.”
Better Auth marks Peak XV’s first direct investment in an African founder.
Engida says Better Auth, currently free to use, will focus on improving its core features and launch a paid enterprise infrastructure that plugs into its open source base. This will give developers the flexibility to self-host or opt for Better Auth’s cloud add-ons as needed.
He’s also thinking about how to scale without trading away the product’s community-built feel. On the roadmap, therefore, is hiring a small team to help maintain the codebase, expand documentation, and support enterprise users. For now, though, Engida is still writing most of the code himself.

data.title: CUDA Ray Tracing 2x Faster Than RTX: My CUDA Ray Tracing Journey
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用CUDA开发了一个比Vulkan/RTX实现更快（快2倍）的光线追踪渲染器。作者通过深入优化，使CUDA版本在相同硬件上性能显著提升，达到了约105 FPS，而Vulkan/RTX版本为约30-50 FPS。性能差异主要源于RTX硬件加速在处理简单程序化几何体（如球体）时效率不高，而CUDA通过纯计算单元处理BVH遍历，减少了内存流量，从而提升了性能。作者的CUDA实现采用了“内联光线追踪”，避免了硬件光线追踪管线的额外开销。尽管这是一个合成场景，且在实际游戏中RTX核心对三角形几何体的处理更高效，但本文展示了在特定条件下纯计算方法的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CUDA光线追踪与RTX性能比较的评论分析

不同观点：
• **esperent**：认为文章标题具有误导性，像点击诱饵。当前标题暗示CUDA光线追踪在所有情况下都比RTX快，但实际上该渲染器可能只能渲染球体，不能处理其他复杂场景。因此，将一个专门优化过的简单渲染器与通用生产渲染器比较是不公平的。

• **sheepscreek**：猜测CUDA模式下使用了GPU的所有计算能力，而RTX模式下GPU计算力可能需要与其他功能共享，从而导致性能差异。

• **kookamamie**：关注技术细节，特别是CUDA中使用`__restrict__`指针的问题，这是C++中缺乏合理的默认别名规则所引发的一个小问题。

• **kachapopopow**：认为绕过渲染后端提高速度并不令人惊讶。同时指出，该实现仅适用于Nvidia的GPU，而Vulkan虽然跨平台兼容性强，但在直接性和性能上与DX11等有所不同，因此仍具有一定的技术参考价值。

• **pixelpoet**：认为文章非常误导，CUDA性能展示中涉及的FMA（熔合乘加）性能实际上并不是关键问题，且RTX单元几乎没有被充分利用，导致比较不公平。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于文章标题和内容的误导性，以及CUDA渲染器与RTX的比较是否公平。
• 技术细节上，有人关注CUDA编程中的特定优化技巧和硬件使用问题。
• 还有讨论涉及不同图形API（如Vulkan和DX11）的跨平台兼容性和性能差异。

44382073.article_content:
CUDA Ray Tracing 2x Faster Than RTX: My CUDA Ray Tracing Journey
Introduction
Welcome! This article is a deep dive into how I made a CUDA-based ray tracer that outperforms a
Vulkan/RTX implementation—sometimes by more than 3x—on the same hardware. If you're interested in
GPU programming, performance optimization, or just want to see how far you can push a path tracer,
you're in the right place.
The comparison is with
RayTracingInVulkan
by GPSnoopy, a well-known Vulkan/RTX renderer. My goal
wasn't just to port
Ray Tracing in One Weekend
to CUDA, but to squeeze every last
millisecond out of it—profiling, analyzing, and optimizing until the numbers surprised even me.
And this is actually how I learned CUDA.
In this write-up, I'll walk you through the journey: what worked, what didn't, and the key
tricks that made the biggest difference. Whether you're a graphics programmer, a CUDA
enthusiast, or just curious about real-world GPU optimization, I hope you'll find something useful
here.
Note
The original title claimed a 3.6x speedup, which was true at the time of writing —
but after
realizing
I forgot to add Russian Roulette to RayTracingInVulkan, the performance difference shrunk to
2x.
Still very significant, and it's more fair now.

restmail -- sendmail for email rest APIs
restmail is a sendmail-compatible CLI using gmail & outlook rest APIs. It can be used
for email automation, notifications and with
git send-mail
for sharing patches.
restmail requires only minimal authorization scope to send mail.  No access to reading
or deleting mail is needed.
Install
# install to ~/go/bin ($GOPATH)
go install github.com/tonymet/restmail@latest
Initial Provider Setup (gmail or outlook)
Initial setup is done once / provider. This configures oauth2 clientID & Secret
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
CLIENT_ID=xxxxxx
CLIENT_SECRET=yyyy
restmail -configClient -provider gmail -clientId "${CLIENT_ID}" \
-clientSecret "${CLIENT_SECRET}" -f "${FROM}"
Authorization Setup
Once provider config is set up above, you need to do the oauth flow through
a web browser.  Setup is only done once or if the tokens are invalidated.
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
restmail -setup -provider gmail -sender "${FROM}"
When this is complete, your auth-token & refresh-token are saved and refreshed
automatically.
Sending Messages
FROM=your.name@gmail.com
TO=friend@gmail.com
CC=billy@gmail.com
echo "subject: test subject\n\ntest messagee" | go run . -f "${FROM} -provider gmail "${TO}" cc:"${CC}"
Git send-mail configuration
[sendemail]
smtpServer = /home/USERNAME/go/bin/restmail
smtpServerOption = -f=your.name@gmail.com
smtpServerOption = -provider
smtpServerOption = gmail

data.title: Anthropic wins fair use victory for AI – but still in trouble for stealing books
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: Anthropic在涉及使用书籍训练AI模型的版权诉讼中获得了一项重大公平使用胜利，但仍面临盗版书籍问题的法律麻烦。2021年，Anthropic的联合创始人Ben Mann下载了包含196,640本盗版书籍的Books3库，并在之后继续下载了其他盗版书籍。尽管公司在2024年转向购买和扫描数百万本实体书，但之前下载的盗版书籍仍保留在其内部研究库中。法官William Alsup的判决认为，扫描的书籍属于公平使用，因为它们仅在公司内部用于训练模型且未对外分享，而下载的电子书不属于公平使用，将面临陪审团审判。法官强调，训练大型语言模型使用未经授权的数据属于公平使用，因为这类似于人类的阅读和创作过程。

• Am4TIfIsER0ppos以讽刺的口吻质疑书籍内容被盗用的具体情况，询问是否涉及书店或出版社的仓库被盗，以此来质疑所谓“偷窃”的定义和实际情形。

Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Anthropic wins a major fair use victory for AI — but it’s still in trouble for stealing books
. Major USA legal news for the AI industry today. Judge William Alsup released a "summary judgement" (a legal decision that results in some parts of a case skipping a trial) in a lawsuit between five authors and Anthropic concerning the use of their books in training data.
The
judgement itself
is a very readable 32 page PDF, and contains all sorts of interesting behind-the-scenes details about how Anthropic trained their models.
The facts of the complaint go back to the very beginning of the company. Anthropic was founded by a group of ex-OpenAI researchers in February 2021. According to the judgement:
So, in January or February 2021, another Anthropic cofounder, Ben Mann, downloaded Books3, an online library of 196,640 books that he knew had been assembled from unauthorized copies of copyrighted books — that is, pirated. Anthropic's next pirated acquisitions involved downloading distributed, reshared copies of other pirate libraries. In June 2021, Mann downloaded in this way at least five million copies of books from Library Genesis, or LibGen, which he knew had been pirated. And, in July 2022, Anthropic likewise downloaded at least two million copies of books from the Pirate Library Mirror, or PiLiMi, which Anthropic knew had been pirated.
Books3 was also listed as
part of the training data
for Meta's first LLaMA model!
Anthropic apparently used these sources of data to help build an internal "research library" of content that they then filtered and annotated and used in training runs.
Books turned out to be a very valuable component of the "data mix" to train strong models. By 2024 Anthropic had a new approach to collecting them: purchase and scan millions of print books!
To find a new way to get books, in February 2024, Anthropic hired the former head of partnerships for Google's book-scanning project, Tom Turvey. He was tasked with obtaining "all the books in the world" while still avoiding as much "legal/practice/business slog" as possible (Opp. Exhs. 21, 27). [...] Turvey and his team emailed major book distributors and retailers about bulk-purchasing their print copies for the AI firm's "research library" (Opp. Exh. 22 at 145; Opp. Exh. 31 at -035589). Anthropic spent many millions of dollars to purchase millions of print books, often in used condition. Then, its service providers stripped the books from their bindings, cut their pages to size, and scanned the books into digital form — discarding the paper originals. Each print book resulted in a PDF copy containing images of the scanned pages with machine-readable text (including front and back cover scans for softcover books).
The summary judgement found that these scanned books
did
fall under fair use, since they were transformative versions of the works and were not shared outside of the company. The downloaded ebooks did
not
count as fair use, and it looks like those will be the subject of a forthcoming jury trial.
Here's that section of the decision:
Before buying books for its central library, Anthropic downloaded over seven million pirated copies of books, paid nothing, and kept these pirated copies in its library even after deciding it would not use them to train its AI (at all or ever again). Authors argue Anthropic should have paid for these pirated library copies (e.g, Tr. 24–25, 65; Opp. 7, 12–13). This
order agrees.
The most important aspect of this case is the question of whether training an LLM on unlicensed data counts as "fair use". The judge found that it did. The argument for why takes up several pages of the document but this seems like a key point:
Everyone reads texts, too, then writes new texts. They may need to pay for getting their hands on a text in the first instance. But to make anyone pay specifically for the use of a book each time they read it, each time they recall it from memory,
each time they later draw upon it when writing new things in new ways would be unthinkable.
For centuries, we have read and re-read books. We have admired, memorized, and internalized
their sweeping themes, their substantive points, and their stylistic solutions to recurring writing problems.
The judge who signed this summary judgement is an interesting character:
William Haskell Alsup
(yes, his middle name really is Haskell) presided over jury trials for Oracle America, Inc. v. Google, Inc in 2012 and 2016 where he famously used his hobbyist BASIC programming experience to challenge claims made by lawyers in the case.

- 法律层面的潜在影响，特别是对正在进行的诉讼可能产生的影响，也被认为是这一问题的重要方面。

data.title: Puerto Rico's Solar Microgrids Beat Blackout
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 文章报道了波多黎各阿洪特斯镇与美国橡树岭国家实验室合作，建立了创新的太阳能微电网系统，以应对频繁的停电问题。这些微电网在一次全岛大停电中成功为当地提供了稳定电力。然而，联邦政府将原本用于太阳能项目的3.65亿美元资金转用于修复传统电网，引发对可再生能源发展受阻的担忧。文章强调了地方在应对气候变化和技术创新上的努力，与联邦政策变动之间的矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭太阳能系统的设计与实施，尤其是在小规模、无需建筑许可、美观以及接线简便等方面的考虑。同时，讨论还涉及到电网同步技术、微电网的应用及其在不同国家和地区的可行性与挑战。

不同观点：
• WillAdams建议建立一个小型太阳能系统，无需建筑许可，通过使用露营用电池组和简单的接线来满足家庭部分电器需求。该方案强调美观和简便。
• tgtweak指出有一种无需转换开关的电网同步逆变器技术，可以降低家庭太阳能系统的入门门槛，但该技术在北美尚未普及。他还提到了波多黎各的微电网互连技术。
• pythonbase提到太阳能在巴基斯坦的广泛应用，尤其是农村和城市地区。
• eagerpace希望有一个解决方案来平滑夏季高峰用电需求，而不必完全依赖太阳能或获得电力公司的信用。
• chilldsgn关注南非频繁停电问题，并提出太阳能解决方案在经济不发达地区的潜力。
• KaiserPro对电网互连失败的规则定义和连接电网所需存储及光伏技术提出疑问。
• m4r1k抱怨在意大利，由于官僚程序，太阳能安装需要数月时间，且自部署方案限制在800瓦以内。
• Simon_O_Rourke认为电池成本是关键问题，并提出预算内的电池解决方案可以应对停电。
• dotancohen解释了家庭太阳能与电网连接的技术问题，包括对电网工人安全和同步化的要求。
• amoshebb批评了微电网和净计量电价政策，认为这些措施仅有利于富裕人群，而无助于整体电网弹性。
• whall6质疑在天气原因导致停电的情况下，太阳能是否能发挥作用。
• danans比较了波多黎各和加利福尼亚的太阳能电池板安装规范，指出加州防火规范限制了全屋顶覆盖。
• greenie_beans预测，由于人工智能的发展，美国电力需求将超过供应，导致电价上涨。
• alexnewman以波多黎各为例，指出依赖太阳能并非万全之策，尤其是在飓风等自然灾害后，太阳能设施的破坏和废弃处理是巨大问题，主张增加基础负荷和天然气使用。
• pyrale批评文章过于偏向太阳能供应商的立场，忽视了电网维护对化石电力行业的必要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于太阳能技术的可行性、成本及其在不同地区和经济条件下的适用性。特别是在波多黎各和其他发展中地区的微电网应用，以及太阳能技术对电网弹性的实际贡献。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是电网同步技术和无需转换开关的逆变器技术在北美和其他地区的普及程度和应用前景。
• 不同国家和地区的法规、天气条件和基础设施状况对太阳能系统的安装和运行产生的影响也是讨论的重要方面。

data.title: The Art of Hanakami, or Flower-Petal Folding
data.author: s4074433
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了使用花瓣作为折纸材料的独特创意，提出了“花纸”（hanakami）这一术语，意指用花瓣代替纸张进行折纸。作者Michael Lai分享了自己多年尝试用各种花瓣折叠不同模型的经验，强调选择合适的花瓣至关重要，需考虑花瓣的形状、大小、颜色、厚度和纹理等因素。由于花瓣不规则且易碎，折叠过程颇具挑战，尤其是压制和干燥环节。工具包括花压器、锋利刀具、切割垫和细头工具等。最终，花瓣能被折成精致的折纸作品，赋予花瓣新的艺术生命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论者对 bougainvillea 花的辨识及其在折纸中使用自然材料的可行性进行了讨论。

不同观点：
• [carlob 的观点]  
   他认为图片中的花非常漂亮，但指出那些不是 bougainvillea 的花瓣。他解释说，bougainvillea 的实际花朵是白色且非常小，无法用于折纸。

• [CuriouKoala 的观点]  
   他对使用自然材料进行折纸表现出浓厚的兴趣，并幽默地提到自己需要一个缩小射线枪来缩小手指以处理这些材料。他表示，用自然材料做折纸是一种有趣的体验，并计划尝试。

补充讨论：
• [对 bougainvillea 花的认知差异]  
   carlob 强调了对于 bougainvillea 花的正确认知，指出许多人可能误解了它的外观，因为它的颜色鲜艳部分其实是苞片，而不是花瓣。

• [对自然材料用于折纸的兴趣]  
   CuriouKoala 更关注于如何将自然材料应用到折纸艺术中，显示出对创新和实验的开放态度。他对于缩小手指的幽默评论也反映了对精细手工操作的挑战意识。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于对 bougainvillea 花的正确辨识上。carlob 强调了花的实际特征，而原始评论可能误解了花的性质。这种认知差异引发了对自然材料在折纸应用中的实际操作性和视觉效果的不同看法。

44350655.article_content:
by
Michael Lai
Edited by
Scott Summers
challenge
plants
folding techniques
What kind of paper would you use to fold flowers?
As folders, we know that finding the right paper for the model we want to fold (and vice versa) is important for achieving the right form and appearance. Personally, I’ve used a lot of different materials for my work, including everything from printer paper and aluminum foil to cellophane, fabric and more.
When folding origami flowers, why not use flower petals?
I first became interested in this idea when my attempts at a Guinness World Record for the smallest origami crane made by hand turned out to be in vain (another story for another time), and I needed something else to make my mark in the origami world.
What started from a thought in my head turned into a labor of love that took me from countless local florists, botanic gardens, herbariums, to the writings of
David Lister,
email correspondence with
Robert Lang
about paper in origami, and now to you, the reader. Suffice to say, I have spent years exploring this unique aspect of our shared craft.
I invite you to read on, learn from my experience, and try it for yourself.
A crane folded from a rose petal by Michael Lai. Photo: Deb Yarrow.
Hanakami: A Definition
How can we describe the folding of flower petals? Certainly, there are no words for it in Japanese or English.
“Orihana,” meaning “folded flower” (折り花) is a strong choice, but I am sure it is already in use. “Hanagami” might be grammatically correct, except that it also means “tissue paper” in Japanese (鼻紙).
However, our emphasis is on the fact that organic materials in the form of flower petals are being substituted for paper.
So, taking the Japanese kanji character for “flower” (花 — hana), and using the same character for “paper” (紙 — kami), we can combine the two words to form “hanakami” (花紙 — hanakami), a portmanteau to mean “using flower as paper,” or “flower paper.”
It is not the folding of flower petal models, but the folding of origami models using flower petals.
No matter what you choose to call it, flower petals can be folded into delicate origami models with intricate details that are revealed when you take a closer look.
A crane’s wing folded from a petal. Photo: Deb Yarrow.
How To Fold Origami From Flowers
By turning a flower petal into an origami model of a flower, we create an abstraction of its original form. In doing so, we provide an alternate way in which the beautiful and delicate petal is given a second life while retaining its natural state.
There is also something to be expected and accepted in the process of folding flower petals, as they are not designed to be square or creased, nor do they come in standard sizes.
Here’s what you’ll need to get started:
Flower petals large enough for the model you want to fold.
A flower press or blotting paper (you can also use any clean and absorbent paper) and something to weigh them down.
A sharp knife (preferably scalpel) to cut the petals.
A cutting mat or something to protect the surface where you cut the petals.
A steel ruler or square (tool).
A fine but round-tipped instrument (knitting needle, crochet hook, chopstick, etc.), if necessary to help with manipulating petals.
Tools used to cut petals fo folding. Photo: Michael Lai.
The fragile nature of a pressed and dried petal adds to the challenge of practicing origami. In addition, because common flower petals are quite small, you’re likely to end up folding smaller origami models.
1. Collect Petals
I personally don’t use flowers in full bloom, as this is their time to shine, and prefer to collect them late in the season, when they have fallen to the ground. Fallen petals also have lower moisture content and are therefore easier and quicker to dry and press. Flowers come in all shapes and sizes, but not all of them are available year-round.
Here are some things to consider when experimenting with different types of flower petals:
Flowering season(s)
Shape and size of petals
Colors and patterns when dried and pressed
Thickness of petals when dried
Surface texture, including density and thickness of veins
Structure and curvature of individual petals
Fragrance
When you are experimenting with different origami models, also consider the following:
Size of model you want to make compared to the size of petals you collect
Difficulty of model and the number of attempts you need compared to the number and availability of petals
Types of folds required compared to the thickness and strength of the petals
Type of pattern for the model compared to the color and pattern on the petals
The primary considerations in selecting the types of flowers to use for origami are based on the physical characteristics of the petals, as determined by color, size, shape, pattern and thickness.
Generally, blooms that are flat, have minimal petals, and aren’t too thick tend to be easiest to prepare and fold. Thinner petals will dry more evenly and are less likely to become moldy during the

• zejn：分享了自己为伴侣制作的地理区域艺术品时间线的经验，强调了将大致日期映射为具体年份的困难。
• bigthymer：简单直接地表达了对项目设计的喜爱。
• jimmydddd：喜欢时间线比较，认为这揭示了历史和科学学习中的孤岛化问题，并通过例子说明不同历史人物的年龄对比如何令人惊讶。
• devdp430：表示对项目的喜爱，建议将哲学进展和时事纳入时间线，并提到计划为气候变化创建时间线。
• blueblimp：享受浏览过程，但指出“哲学与艺术”行在1890年后没有内容。
• sebastianlay：对可视化表示赞赏，建议寻找1800年前的战争死亡数据以进行比较，并提出让图标和标签保持固定的实用建议。

主要讨论点：围绕AI营销及其目标群体的讨论

不同观点：
• [bni] 认为对AI印象深刻的多为“傻瓜”，因此AI的核心受众是那些容易被营销打动的人，属于“低垂的果实”（指容易获取的目标客户）。

• [8bitsrule] 指出广告商长期以来通过操纵人们的社交恐惧和焦虑来进行营销，这种策略从上世纪就已经开始，例如通过宣传让女性为了形象而去吸烟。评论中将这种现象与AI营销进行类比，暗示类似的操纵手法正在被使用。

• [rasz] 提出AI营销是一种过滤机制，类似于微软的那篇“为什么尼日利亚骗子说他们来自尼日利亚”文章中所描述的过滤骗局。这意味着AI相关的宣传可以筛选出特定类型的人群，那些容易轻信或上当的人。

• [hammyhavoc] 质疑AI解决方案是否通过“dogfooding”（即公司内部使用自己的技术）来设计和测试，并暗示这种方法可能不完全适合其目标受众。

• [orionblastar] 提供了一个MIT关于AI和智力的研究链接，试图将讨论引向更学术或科学的方向，可能意在提供关于AI更深层次的理解。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI营销是否刻意针对易受操纵的群体，以及这种做法是否道德或有效。
• 讨论中提到了历史上的广告案例，表明类似的营销策略早已存在，且一直利用人们的恐惧和焦虑。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对AI技术是否通过自身体验（dogfooding）来改进和适配目标用户的质疑。

data.title: Howdy – Windows Hello style facial authentication for Linux
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: Howdy 是一个为 Linux 提供类似 Windows Hello™ 面部认证功能的软件。它利用内置的红外发射器和摄像头进行面部识别，通过 PAM 系统实现登录、锁屏、sudo 等场景下的密码替代。Howdy 支持 Debian/Ubuntu、Arch Linux、Fedora 和 openSUSE 等发行版，安装方式各有不同，部分需要额外配置。它依赖于 Python 3.6+、meson、ninja 等工具构建，并可通过命令行管理面部模型。安装后需运行 `sudo howdy add` 进行面部录入。如遇问题，可通过查看 Wiki 或 GitHub 上的类似问题进行排查。用户还可以通过贡献代码或提交功能请求参与项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源面部识别认证项目的质量和功能与商业版本的比较，以及技术实现和应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• **[bsimpson]** 认为开源项目的面部识别认证可能会有更多的误报/漏报，因为商业版本需要支持所有人使用，经过了大量测试，而开源项目可能在广泛适用性上有所欠缺。

• **[aitchnyu]** 关注用户体验问题，希望在系统处理面部识别时有提示，特别是当识别失败时，可以有一个重试按钮。同时，也对红外照片是否会欺骗模型提出了疑问，并对红外摄像头的实验表示兴趣。

• **[joelthelion]** 表示希望能有更好的指纹识别支持，暗示面部识别并不是其首选的认证方式。

• **[charcircuit]** 指出该开源项目与Windows Hello的不同之处，包括它仅通过2D图像提取特征，缺乏深度重建，容易被纸张等简单手段欺骗。此外，还提到该项目在功能上不如Windows的面部识别广泛，仅用于用户认证，且保存面部特征点文件时使用明文，存在安全问题。

• **[mouse_]** 表达了对预桌面认证功能的期待，认为这是一个非常吸引人的特性，希望能看到其实现。

• **[seany]** 关注开源面部识别模型在NIST/iBeta排名中达到较好性能所需的条件，暗示开源项目在性能上与商业模型存在差距。

• **[deafpolygon]** 对项目依赖Python2表示不解，可能在考虑技术更新和维护的必要性。

• **[fsateler]** 注意到项目虽然活跃，但最后一个版本发布于2020年，质疑为何没有新的版本发布。

补充讨论：
• 项目在技术实现上的局限性（如2D图像 vs 深度重建）以及安全性问题（明文保存特征点）是主要的技术争议点。
• 用户体验和多因素认证方式（如指纹识别与面部识别的对比）也是讨论的重要内容。
• 开源项目与商业版本在性能、可靠性及功能广泛性上的对比是潜在的争议焦点。

Howdy provides Windows Hello™ style authentication for Linux. Use your built-in IR emitters and camera in combination with facial recognition to prove who you are.
Using the central authentication system (PAM), this works everywhere you would otherwise need your password: Login, lock screen, sudo, su, etc.
Installation
Howdy is currently available and packaged for Debian/Ubuntu, Arch Linux, Fedora and openSUSE. If you’re interested in packaging Howdy for your distro, don’t hesitate to open an issue.
Note:
The build of dlib can hang on 100% for over a minute, give it time.
Ubuntu or Linux Mint
Run the installer by pasting (
ctrl+shift+V
) the following commands into the terminal one at a time:
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:boltgolt/howdy
sudo apt update
sudo apt install howdy
This will guide you through the installation.
Debian
Download the .deb file from the
Releases page
and install with gdebi.
Arch Linux
Maintainer wanted.
Install the
howdy
package from the AUR. For AUR installation instructions, take a look at this
wiki page
.
You will need to do some additional configuration steps. Please read the
ArchWiki entry
for more information.
Fedora
Maintainer:
@luyatshimbalanga
The
howdy
package is available as a
Fedora COPR repository
, install it by simply executing the following commands in a terminal:
sudo dnf copr enable principis/howdy
sudo dnf --refresh install howdy
Note:
Fedora 41
removed support for Python2
, but at this point in time Howdy still depends on it. If the install fails, you can fix this by installing the beta Repository and removing the release version:
sudo dnf copr remove principis/howdy
sudo dnf copr enable principis/howdy-beta
sudo dnf --refresh install howdy
See the link to the COPR repository for detailed configuration steps.
openSUSE
Maintainer:
@dmafanasyev
Go to the
openSUSE wiki page
for detailed installation instructions.
Building from source
If you want to build Howdy from source, a few dependencies are required.
Dependencies
Python 3.6 or higher
pip
setuptools
wheel
meson version 0.64 or higher
ninja
INIReader (can be pulled from git automatically if not found)
libevdev
To install them on Debian/Ubuntu for example:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y \
python3 python3-pip python3-setuptools python3-wheel \
cmake make build-essential \
libpam0g-dev libinih-dev libevdev-dev python3-opencv \
python3-dev libopencv-dev
Build
meson setup build
meson compile -C build
You can also install Howdy to your system with
meson install -C build
.
Setup
After installation, Howdy needs to learn what you look like so it can recognise you later. Run
sudo howdy add
to add a face model.
If nothing went wrong we should be able to run sudo by just showing your face. Open a new terminal and run
sudo -i
to see it in action. Please check
this wiki page
if you're experiencing problems or
search
for similar issues.
If you're curious you can run
sudo howdy config
to open the central config file and see the options Howdy has to offer. On most systems this will open the nano editor, where you have to press
ctrl
+
x
to save your changes.
CLI
The installer adds a
howdy
command to manage face models for the current user. Use
howdy --help
or
man howdy
to list the available options.
Usage:
howdy [-U user] [-y] command [argument]
Command
Description
add
Add a new face model for a user
clear
Remove all face models for a user
config
Open the config file in your default editor
disable
Disable or enable howdy
list
List all saved face models for a user
remove
Remove a specific model for a user
snapshot
Take a snapshot of your camera input
test
Test the camera and recognition methods
version
Print the current version number
Contributing
The easiest ways to contribute to Howdy is by starring the repository and opening GitHub issues for features you'd like to see. If you want to do more, you can also
buy me a coffee
.
Code contributions are also very welcome. If you want to port Howdy to another distro, feel free to open an issue for that too.
Troubleshooting
Any Python errors get logged directly into the console and should indicate what went wrong. If authentication still fails but no errors are printed, you could take a

data.title: Build a Sentence-Level Text-to-Speech Reader in JavaScript
data.author: javatuts
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用JavaScript构建一个具有句子级高亮和文本语音合成（TTS）功能的网页阅读工具。主要内容包括：

1. **TTS实现**：利用浏览器的`SpeechSynthesis` API，通过`SpeechSynthesisUtterance`对象控制语音播放，支持选择语音和调整播放参数（如语速、音高）。
2. **句子高亮**：使用CSS和JavaScript动态高亮当前朗读的句子。
3. **功能整合**：创建一个包含播放、暂停、恢复、停止按钮的阅读工具，并实现句子逐句朗读和高亮。

文章提供了完整的HTML结构、CSS样式和JavaScript逻辑代码示例，帮助开发者构建一个交互式的TTS阅读器。

Build a Sentence-Level Reader with JS TTS & Highlights June, 23rd 2025 5 min read In this article, we’ll build a simple web tool to explore how Text-to-Speech (TTS) works in JavaScript. We’ll also dive into the logic of sentence-level highlighting . These two features are often combined to create accessible, dynamic reading experiences in the browser. We’ll go step-by-step: Learn how TTS works in the browser Explore how to highlight sentences dynamically Build a working mini tool with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript ( Demo & Code ) 📢 What is TTS in the browser? JavaScript provides built-in support for speech synthesis using the SpeechSynthesis API. It allows us to speak text out loud using voices available in the system. Core objects: speechSynthesis — controller to play, pause, stop, and resume speech SpeechSynthesisUtterance — represents the text that will be spoken ✨ Simple example: js Copy Copied! 1 2 const msg = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance("Hello, world!"); window.speechSynthesis.speak(msg); ⚙️ Add voice and settings: js Copy Copied! 1 2 3 4 5 6 const utter = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance("This is a test"); const voices = window.speechSynthesis.getVoices(); utter.voice = voices.find(v => v.lang === 'en-US'); utter.rate = 1.2; utter.pitch = 1; window.speechSynthesis.speak(utter); You can also track when speech starts and ends: js Copy Copied! 1 2 utter.onstart = () => console.log('Started speaking'); utter.onend = () => console.log('Finished speaking'); ✍️ Sentence-level Highlighting To show which sentence is currently being read, we’ll highlight that sentence using CSS and JavaScript. data.title: Games That Weren't: Preserving Cancelled and Unreleased Video Game History
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了几个经典游戏的原型和保存情况：

1. **Alien 3 C64原型**：一个罕见的Commodore 64版《Alien 3》演示原型最近被发现，可能是用于展示项目进展或提供给杂志刊登截图，但未被正式包含在当时的杂志demo中。

2. **Carts of Fury保存**：2007年的Flash游戏《Carts of Fury》原本在线提供，后被物理保存并数字化，上传至档案网站。

3. **Dr. Franken 3**：1993年Game Boy游戏《Dr. Franken》系列的第三部作品原型被发现，游戏风格与前作大不相同，涉及太空冒险和解谜。

4. **Legacy of the Fallen**：1999年为《Shogo: Mobile Armor Division》开发的扩展包，由Anarchy Arts开发，团队在全球不同地点协作，最终在盐湖城集中开发完成。

5. **The Last Stuntman**：1989年CRL计划发布的游戏，分为6个部分，由不同开发者制作，目前仅有Amiga版截图被找到。

6. **World Class Rugby SNES原型**：1992年《World Class Rugby》SNES原型被发现，使用不同的引擎和视角，与最终版本有显著差异。

这些发现对游戏历史保存和研究具有重要意义。

Legacy of the Fallen
Posted:

by

1999 Anarchy Arts
Platform: PC
Also known as: Shogo: Mobile Armor Division Expansion Pack – Legacy of the Fallen
Legacy of the Fallen was an ambitious add-on pack developed by Anarchy Arts as an expansion for the 1998 first-person shooter
Shogo: Mobile Armor Division
. The project began in late 1998 after Monolith Productions, the creators of Shogo, approached Anarchy Arts with an offer to develop the add-on. For the relatively young and unknown studio, this was an exciting opportunity to make a name and earn revenue, so they accepted.
Anarchy Arts operated initially as a virtual company with team members scattered worldwide, but the scale of the project led them to consolidate in Salt Lake City, Utah. There, the core team of about ten people, including programmers, level designers, and artists lived and worked intensely for seven months in a cramped three bedroom apartment, putting in long hours to bring Legacy of the Fallen to life. The development was powered by Monolith’s LithTech engine, which the team praised for its flexibility despite some early challenges.

data.title: Why DARPA Thinks Stealth Is Obsolete in Future Wars
data.author: nradov
data.article_summary: DARPA认为，随着量子传感技术的快速发展，隐形技术在未来战争中的价值正逐渐减弱。国防高级研究计划局（DARPA）副局长Rob McHenry表示，传感器融合和人工智能的进步使得大规模隐形不再现实。未来战争将更依赖速度、自我防御和规避技术。虽然美国空军正投资于新一代隐形战机，但DARPA正在探索提高速度、机动性和抗损伤能力的方案。McHenry强调，需加强空中防御能力，如为战机配备反导弹系统。此外，量子传感技术能精确探测隐形目标，正从科学研究转向实际应用。DARPA还在研究高超音速武器和平台，并重新审视高超音速项目的投资，以应对未来战场需求。
