44389816.article_content:
Huntington
Verso
The Huntington’s blog takes you behind the scenes for a scholarly view of the collections.
E.A. Spitzka’s Studies of Exceptional and Deviant Brains
Posted on
Tue., Dec. 3, 2024
by
Joel A.
Klein, Ph.D.
Previous slide
Next slide
Edward Anthony Spitzka, from
Empire State Notables, 1914
(New York: Hartwell Stafford, 1914).
| Library of Congress.
Edward Anthony Spitzka (1876–1922) was a fourth-year medical student at Columbia University when he gained national attention for performing the autopsy of Leon Czolgosz, the man executed for assassinating President William McKinley. Spitzka, an emerging figure in neuroanatomy and brain morphology, was undoubtedly selected for this prominent task due to his father, Edward Charles Spitzka, who had testified on the insanity of Charles Guiteau, President James Garfield’s assassin, nearly a quarter-century earlier.
Previous slide
Next slide
1
of
3
Mugshots of Leon Czolgosz, ca. September 1901, after he shot President McKinley.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
E.A. Spitzka’s postmortem drawing of Czolgosz’s brain, Oct. 29, 1901. Spitzka’s examination of Czolgosz’s brain revealed no major abnormalities and provided no indication that he was insane at the time of the assassination.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Newspaper clipping illustrating Czolgosz’s final moments. Edward Anthony Spitzka and Edward Charles Spitzka papers.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
The younger Spitzka’s career flourished after he took a position at Thomas Jefferson University in Philadelphia, where he gained recognition for his studies on the relationship between brain structures and behavior. His particular interest lay in the extremes of human nature—both pathological and extraordinary—and he sought to understand the physiology behind deviance and brilliance. In addition to his academic pursuits, Spitzka served as the editor of the 1910 edition of
Gray’s Anatomy
, one of the most authoritative medical texts of the time.
The Huntington is fortunate to hold a substantial collection of the Spitzkas’ personal and professional papers, which provide a window into a transformative period in neuroscience, psychology, and American history. Before The Huntington’s acquisition, the collection remained largely unexplored, but ongoing research is beginning to shed light on its significance and much remains to be discovered.
E.A. Spitzka’s fascination with the brain led him to conduct postmortem examinations on several notable individuals, including Major John Wesley Powell, the renowned geologist, soldier, and explorer best known for his leadership of the United States Geological Survey.
Left: C.C. Pierce,
Major John Wesley Powell
. Right: E.A. Spitzka’s pencil drawing of Powell’s brain.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Spitzka was also intrigued by the brain of George Francis Train, a wealthy American businessman famous for his eccentric behavior and grandiose claims, including his assertion that he had inspired Jules Verne’s
Around the World in Eighty Days
and his declaration that he was the “dictator of the United States.” Spitzka even had the opportunity to study the brain of the poet Walt Whitman, though no formal analysis was produced after the specimen was accidentally dropped in the lab and shattered.
E.A. Spitzka’s tracing of a drawing of George Francis Train’s brain superimposed on Spitzka’s sketch of Train’s profile, made during an autopsy.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
The collection also documents Spitzka’s numerous visits to Northeastern prisons to attend executions and perform postmortem examinations on murderers, as he sought to uncover the biological roots of criminality. Among the most famous cases is that of Chester Gillette, who was convicted of murdering his pregnant girlfriend, Grace Brown, in 1906 by striking her with a tennis racket and leaving her to drown in Big Moose Lake in upstate New York. His sensational trial became the basis for Theodore Dreiser’s novel
An American Tragedy
.
Spitzka’s postmortem study of Chester Gillette’s brain drew widespread public attention, as evidenced by this full-page spread from a 1908 edition of the tabloid the American Examiner, which catered primarily to British expatriates in the United States.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Other significant cases in the collection include that of Frank Henry Burness, who murdered ship captain George Townsend in 1903 over a pay dispute and later confessed to killing at least nine other people.
Left: Clipping from the New York Herald about Frank Henry Burness’ execution. Right: An information card from Burness’ execution.
| The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens.
Also documented is the case of the Van Wormer brothers—Willis, Frederick, and Burton—who murdered their wealthy uncle, Peter Hallenbeck, in 1901 aft

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lovable及类似LLM驱动软件工具的潜力和局限

不同观点：
• Workaccount2认为LLM工具（如Lovable）能够有效解决传统软件功能臃肿、学习曲线陡峭的问题。通过LLM，非技术用户可以根据具体需求定制简单工具，避免购买昂贵的综合软件包。他以自己使用Gemini创建CAD文件转换工具为例，说明LLM如何简化开发流程。
• B0a04gl强调了LLM工具在捕捉用户产品思维和决策过程方面的潜力，认为如果能够记录和回放用户的操作和编辑理由，将形成宝贵的“应用决策记忆”，为产品开发提供长期价值。
• Asdev对Lovable的商业模式表示怀疑，认为其用户主要用于构建原型，项目完成度在60-70%后往往被放弃，导致高流失率。他质疑Lovable能否通过现有模式持续盈利。
• Logifail对“Lovable能构建所有其他软件”的说法表示怀疑，认为这种宣传过于夸张。
• Clvx指出Lovable等工具在可靠性和“Day 2操作”（即部署后的维护和扩展）上的不足，认为这些工具需要更好地整合生态系统以提高盈利能力。
• Jun8对Lovable的当前定价策略提出质疑，认为其可能过于便宜，旨在快速获取大量用户。他提到Lovable可以通过创建应用商店等手段增加收入。
• Nichochar分享了作为业内人士的观点，指出Lovable的用户流失率高且面临与其他服务（如Supabase）的合作问题，未来可能需要通过自建生态系统来解决问题。
• Maest对过度宣传Lovable的现象表示反感，认为相关内容往往言过其实。
• Exiguus认为Lovable在非技术用户中受欢迎，但对其能否满足专业开发需求持怀疑态度，认为其主要适合原型设计而非完整产品开发。
• Socketcluster介绍了自己的项目Saasufy，强调了专注于无服务器部分的策略，并指出AI公司正努力确保用户不绕过其聊天界面。
• Chaosprint对Lovable的订阅模式提出疑问，认为对于年轻公司而言，月度经常性收入（MRR）可能比年度经常性收入（ARR）更重要。
• Janalsncm分享了自己使用Lovable构建应用框架的经验，认为其在简单项目中表现出色，但在处理复杂项目时存在不足。
• Fokamul幽默地表示支持在企业环境中使用LLM工具，并预测网络安全将在2026年蓬勃发展。
• _Pdp_认为LLM工具目前主要用于创建简单应用，与之前的工具相比并无突破性进展，且软件开发的核心挑战在于维护而非编写新代码。

补充讨论：
• 关于Lovable的商业模式是否可持续存在争议，主要集中在用户流失率高和项目完成度低的问题。
• 多位评论者提到Lovable等工具在处理复杂项目和“Day 2操作”上的不足，认为需要加强生态系统整合和功能可靠性。
• 部分评论者对Lovable的过度宣传表示反感，认为其宣传内容往往言过其实。
• 一些评论者分享了作为业内人士的观点，指出Lovable在市场定位和商业策略上面临的挑战。

• B0a04gl强调了LLM工具在捕捉用户产品思维和决策过程方面的潜力，认为如果能够记录和回放用户的操作和编辑理由，将形成宝贵的“应用决策记忆”，为产品开发提供长期价值。
• Asdev对Lovable的商业模式表示怀疑，认为其用户主要用于构建原型，项目完成度在60-70%后往往被放弃，导致高流失率。他质疑Lovable能否通过现有模式持续盈利。
• Logifail对“Lovable能构建所有其他软件”的说法表示怀疑，认为这种宣传过于夸张。
• Clvx指出Lovable等工具在可靠性和“Day 2操作”（即部署后的维护和扩展）上的不足，认为这些工具需要更好地整合生态系统以提高盈利能力。
• Jun8对Lovable的当前定价策略提出质疑，认为其可能过于便宜，旨在快速获取大量用户。他提到Lovable可以通过创建应用商店等手段增加收入。
• Nichochar分享了作为业内人士的观点，指出Lovable的用户流失率高且面临与其他服务（如Supabase）的合作问题，未来可能需要通过自建生态系统来解决问题。
• Maest对过度宣传Lovable的现象表示反感，认为相关内容往往言过其实。
• Exiguus认为Lovable在非技术用户中受欢迎，但对其能否满足专业开发需求持怀疑态度，认为其主要适合原型设计而非完整产品开发。

主要讨论点：AR/VR技术在各行业应用的现状、挑战与前景

不同观点：
• **AR技术在工业质量控制中的应用**：
   - isk517认为Hololens 2在质量控制(QC)中表现出色，能够提升工作效率和准确性。
   - 然而，他指出大公司对AR兴趣不足，Hololens 2硬件能力接近极限，技术尚未完全成熟。
   - 他还提到AR的核心价值是提升人工操作的效率，但科技公司更关注AI而非实用工具。

• **AR/VR设备在实际工作中的局限性**：
   - idkwhattocallme指出过去十年AR/VR设备存在重量、价格、易碎性、电池寿命短等问题。
   - 许多客户发现这些设备在实际操作中不如智能手机方便，主要用于查阅手册或通话。
   - 近期语音技术(LLMs)和Meta的“眼镜形态”设备重新引发了大公司的兴趣，正在探索新的应用场景如检查和表格填写。

• **VR设备在办公环境中的不适与健康风险**：
   - edent认为即使忽略费用和卫生问题，VR头戴设备仍会导致部分用户不适，且长时间佩戴不舒适、孤立感强。
   - 这些因素限制了VR在办公环境中的广泛应用。

• **AR技术在远程协助和培训中的成功案例**：
   - lormayna分享了在能源服务公司使用VR进行远程协助和培训的成功案例，显著节省了时间和成本。

• **消费级AR设备的使用体验**：
   - gavinray和j-wags分享了个人使用Viture Pro XR和TCL Rayneo Air 2显示眼镜的体验，指出了设备设计和舒适度方面的问题。
   - 他们期待未来AR设备的改进和更多市场选择。

• **AR/VR在工程和建筑行业中的应用挑战**：
   - ugolino91提到AR/VR平台在工程和建筑行业中仍面临硬件限制，不能完全替代传统PC工作流。
   - 这些设备只能在特定场景下使用，尚需与2D显示器配合。

• **特定场景下的AR需求与设备限制**：
   - wiseleo指出在复杂工作场景（如高空作业）中，AR技术有实际需求，但目前设备尚未普及。
   - spookie提到AR设备在特殊职业培训（如消防员）中面临电池寿命和耐用性的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **企业对AR/VR设备的接受度与投资回报**：
   - SomeUserName432提到Equinor（挪威石油公司）使用Hololens的成功案例。
   - curiouscavalier指出AR/VR在培训中的应用比公众认知的要广泛，但在实际操作中面临设备可靠性和工作流程改变的阻力。
   - 企业对AR/VR的ROI（投资回报）和设备适应性仍持观望态度，许多决策者缺乏实际使用经验。

• **远程工作与便携式虚拟桌面环境的探索**：
   - geocrasher提到正在考虑使用Oculus 3作为便携式虚拟桌面环境，以替代大型显示器，适应远程工作需求。

• **AR/VR在CAD数据可视化中的潜力与挑战**：
   - jlarocco指出其公司在CAD数据翻译工具中尝试支持VR眼镜，但后续进展不大，主要挑战在于是否能为客户带来足够的价值。

争议焦点：
• **AR/VR设备是否能在实际工作中广泛应用**：
   - 一方面，支持者认为AR/VR在特定行业和场景中能显著提升效率和降低成本。
   - 另一方面，批评者指出设备的技术限制、使用不便和市场接受度低等问题，认为科技公司应更关注实用性而非创新噱头。

data.title: Deep Down the Rabbit Hole: Bash, OverlayFS, and a 30-Year-Old Surprise
data.author: Deeg9rie9usi
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了一次调试过程，涉及Bash、OverlayFS以及一个30年前的意外问题。最初，客户报告在切换到OverlayFS后，OpenSSH的scp命令失败，错误信息显示为"shell-init: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Inappropriate ioctl for device"。经过分析，发现问题出在Bash自己的getcwd()实现上，而非glibc或内核问题。

调查发现，Bash在编译时由于交叉编译环境问题，错误地认为系统的getcwd()不可用，从而使用了内部的备用实现。这个备用实现是为缺乏现代功能的旧系统设计的，不适用于OverlayFS。具体来说，OverlayFS在处理目录inode时与Bash的旧算法不兼容，导致错误。

最终，通过参考Yocto项目的做法，明确配置bash_cv_getcwd_malloc解决此问题。修复后，错误消失，问题得到解决。

主要讨论点：POSIX API中errno和相关函数的复杂性及其导致的长期未被发现的bug，以及跨平台配置工具（如autoconf）的问题。

不同观点：
• **chubot**：认为POSIX API在处理errno时令人沮丧，通常不需要手动设置errno，但在某些情况下（如readdir()）则需要。他还提到在开发Oils项目时发现并修复了一个与$PWD相关的bug，这个问题在AT&T ksh中存在了30多年。他还指出shell不能单纯依赖getcwd()，需要结合继承的$PWD和当前值来判断路径。

• **JonChesterfield**：对bug报告的回应感到失望。修复方法是设置errno=0以确保错误信息合理，但回应中却有人以“文件系统不应这样工作”为由提出反对意见。

• **jwilk**：提供了相关的bug报告链接，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **justincormack**：认为configure脚本中的检查大多已经过时，尤其在跨平台编译时容易出问题。很多系统已经禁用了一些老旧的检查，比如Nix在2017年所做的更改。

• **saurik**：指出在交叉编译时，忽略警告并依赖默认设置是不可取的。开发者应该更仔细地处理配置问题，要么手动提供autoconf所需的信息，要么确保能在目标系统上运行二进制文件。

• **malkia**：认为autoconf虽然表面上看起来容易使用，但实际会以难以理清的方式出错。他更倾向于针对特定平台进行有限配置，以确保编译时明确知道哪些定义可用，而不是猜测主机环境。

• **pogopop77**：认为这是一个有趣的调查，展示了新的文件系统范式（如overlay filesystems）如何微妙地影响行为，导致难以追踪的复杂问题。

• **akoboldfrying**：以幽默方式指出，软件开发中需要考虑的不仅是某个条件是否满足，还要考虑各种其他因素（如特定操作系统问题），暗示开发的复杂性。

• **x0x0**：认为这个问题说明了软件开发的困难。长期以来，readdir()的inode号码有特定语义，但支持overlay文件系统需要改变这些语义，而大量软件是基于旧语义开发的，导致升级困难。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于POSIX API设计是否合理，尤其是在errno处理和readdir()函数的行为上。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是autoconf等跨平台配置工具在现代开发环境中的局限性和问题。
- 评论中多次提到历史遗留问题，如30多年未修复的bug，反映出软件维护的长尾效应。

Deep Down the Rabbit Hole: Bash, OverlayFS, and a 30-Year-Old Surprise
This blog post recounts a recent debugging session that uncovered a surprising set of issues involving Bash,
getcwd()
1
, and OverlayFS
2
.
What began as a simple customer bug report evolved into a deep dive worth sharing.
Initial Bug Report
A customer reported that OpenSSH scp
3
failed after switching to OverlayFS.
We found the following error in the logs:
shell-init: error retrieving current directory: \
getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Inappropriate ioctl for device
After analyzing the report, we realized the message didn’t come from scp itself but from the Bash shell.
We asked the key question: why couldn’t Bash determine the current working directory, and why did it fail with
ENOTTY
(Inappropriate ioctl for device)?
Ruling Out the Kernel
Because the issue appeared after the introduction of OverlayFS, we reviewed the OverlayFS source code in the Linux kernel for any code paths that return
ENOTTY
.
Although such paths exist, we considered hitting them highly unlikely.
Bash uses glibc and is written in C.
We examined the glibc system call wrapper for
getcwd()
but found no logic that could return
ENOTTY
.
The wrapper mainly handles buffer allocation and falls back to a generic implementation if the system call fails.
To test this theory, we enabled system call tracing.
Surprisingly, the trace revealed that the
getcwd()
system call never got called.
Since glibc offers multiple
getcwd()
implementations depending on the system, we double-checked that we had reviewed the correct Linux-specific one.
We found no code path that bypassed the system call.
Bash’s home made
getcwd()
A hunch led us to check how Bash links to the
getcwd
symbol:
$ nm -D bash | grep getcwd
...
000c7b10 T getcwd
...
This showed that Bash includes its own
getcwd()
function rather than relying on glibc’s version.
We expected this output instead:
$ nm -D bash | grep getcwd
...
U getcwd
...
Surprised, we inspected the Bash source and confirmed it does contain a
getcwd()
implementation, but guarded by the following:
#if !defined (HAVE_GETCWD)
Developers originally intended this fallback for ancient Unix systems lacking the
getcwd()
system call.
On Linux,
HAVE_GETCWD
should normally be defined.
We confirmed in
config.h
:
#define HAVE_GETCWD 1
At first, this puzzled us because under normal conditions, the implementation should never compile.
But further inspection of
config-bot.h
showed this logic:
#if defined (HAVE_GETCWD) && defined (GETCWD_BROKEN) && !defined (SOLARIS)
#  undef HAVE_GETCWD
#endif
Sure enough, our
config.h
defined
GETCWD_BROKEN
.
That explained why Bash used its internal fallback.
But why did the system consider
getcwd()
broken?
Cross-Compilation Confusion
We examined the output of the
configure
script in detail to trace the origin of
GETCWD_BROKEN
.
We found this line:
checking if getcwd() will dynamically allocate memory with 0 size... \
configure: WARNING: cannot check whether getcwd allocates memory when cross-compiling \
-- defaulting to no
The check in
aclocal.m4
sets
GETCWD_BROKEN
if it can’t confirm that
getcwd()
allocates memory with a zero-size buffer.
Since the build occurred in a cross-compilation environment, the test defaulted to failure.
We discovered that Bash becomes problematic in cross-compilation environments.
Since Bash is cross-compiled for ARM in this specific setup, this made sense.
We then wondered why this issue wasn’t more widespread.
After all, both Bash and OverlayFS are common in embedded systems.
Next, we looked into how major embedded Linux projects like Yocto handle cross-compiling Bash.
Although the Bash Yocto recipe didn’t mention
getcwd
, we found this line in
meta/site/common-glibc
:
bash_cv_getcwd_malloc
=
${
bash_cv_getcwd_malloc
=yes
}
Yocto explicitly overrides the test result to avoid the fallback.
The embedded Linux build system we used didn’t apply such a workaround.
This clarified the issue.
After we implemented a similar override, the issue vanished.
Root Cause Analysis
At this point, we had identified and fixed the bug.
But several questions remained:
Why did the issue appear only with OverlayFS?
Why did Bash’s fallback
getcwd()
fail?
During testing, we observed another error message:
shell-init: error retrieving current directory: \
getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Success
This indicated that
errno
was sometimes set to
0
, suggesting no error occurred, yet
getcwd()
still failed.
OverlayFS and Inode Numbers
To answer the remaining questions, we analyzed Bash’s
getcwd()
implementation.
On Linux, you can determine the current working directory in two ways:
Use the
getcwd()
system call
Read the
/proc/self/cwd
symlink
Bash’s implementation used neither, aiming to support systems lacking these features.
In fact, the fallback dates back to the last millennium.
It used a classic Unix algorithm to reconstruct the working directory path:
I

• **chubot**：认为POSIX API在处理errno时令人沮丧，通常不需要手动设置errno，但在某些情况下（如readdir()）则需要。他还提到在开发Oils项目时发现并修复了一个与$PWD相关的bug，这个问题在AT&T ksh中存在了30多年。他还指出shell不能单纯依赖getcwd()，需要结合继承的$PWD和当前值来判断路径。

• **JonChesterfield**：对bug报告的回应感到失望。修复方法是设置errno=0以确保错误信息合理，但回应中却有人以“文件系统不应这样工作”为由提出反对意见。

• **jwilk**：提供了相关的bug报告链接，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **justincormack**：认为configure脚本中的检查大多已经过时，尤其在跨平台编译时容易出问题。很多系统已经禁用了一些老旧的检查，比如Nix在2017年所做的更改。

• **saurik**：指出在交叉编译时，忽略警告并依赖默认设置是不可取的。开发者应该更仔细地处理配置问题，要么手动提供autoconf所需的信息，要么确保能在目标系统上运行二进制文件。

• **malkia**：认为autoconf虽然表面上看起来容易使用，但实际会以难以理清的方式出错。他更倾向于针对特定平台进行有限配置，以确保编译时明确知道哪些定义可用，而不是猜测主机环境。

• **pogopop77**：认为这是一个有趣的调查，展示了新的文件系统范式（如overlay filesystems）如何微妙地影响行为，导致难以追踪的复杂问题。

• **akoboldfrying**：以幽默方式指出，软件开发中需要考虑的不仅是某个条件是否满足，还要考虑各种其他因素（如特定操作系统问题），暗示开发的复杂性。

• **x0x0**：认为这个问题说明了软件开发的困难。长期以来，readdir()的inode号码有特定语义，但支持overlay文件系统需要改变这些语义，而大量软件是基于旧语义开发的，导致升级困难。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于POSIX API设计是否合理，尤其是在errno处理和readdir()函数的行为上。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是autoconf等跨平台配置工具在现代开发环境中的局限性和问题。
- 评论中多次提到历史遗留问题，如30多年未修复的bug，反映出软件维护的长尾效应。

data.title: How to Write Compelling Release Announcements
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何改进发布公告的撰写，使其更关注用户体验而非技术细节。文章指出，许多发布公告仅简单罗列新功能，像 changelog 一样，缺乏对用户实际使用场景的描述。好的发布公告应强调新功能对用户的实际好处，使用户感到兴奋。例如，不要只说添加了“重复”按钮，而要说明用户可以用此按钮创建定期事件，简化操作。发布公告应突出对用户体验影响最大的变化，而非技术实现细节。此外，公告还应简要介绍产品，吸引新用户，同时不忽视现有用户。最后，避免使用“各种改进和错误修复”这样模糊的表述。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何撰写发布公告和发布说明，特别是在内容详尽程度、营销语气和用户关注点之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• **支持详尽的发布说明**：
  - lapcat认为发布说明应尽量详尽，包括所有修复的bug和新引入的问题，以便用户了解软件的变化。
  - 作为独立开发者，lapcat的用户对详尽的发布说明表示赞赏。
  - 反对将发布说明用于营销目的，认为这是对用户的烦扰。

• **支持简明、用户导向的发布公告**：
  - deanebarker和loughnane支持简明扼要的发布公告，强调直接说明实际变化，而非包装成营销信息。
  - loughnane建议通过减少文字来避免读者失去兴趣，例如“Create events 10x faster”的示例。

• **平衡详尽与简明**：
  - deanebarker建议可以有两套说明：一套简明的基础说明，另一套较为详细的“润色”说明。
  - ednite认为发布公告应结合用户体验透明地说明修复和改进，同时建议维护一份详细的技术 changelog 以供内部参考。

• **关注营销与用户价值**：
  - ukuina和chapz批评过度营销化的发布公告，认为这忽视了实际的用户需求。
  - flpm和thewisenerd则认为发布公告应强调对用户的价值，并通过选择性 spotlight 最重要的改进以吸引用户注意。

• **关于具体示例和数值描述的争议**：
  - awkward提醒对具体数值应谨慎使用，以免误导不成熟的用户或被成熟用户识破夸大。
  - jcalx强调写作应根据用户实际需求和痛点进行，避免不必要的技术细节和数字描述。

补充讨论：
• **发布公告的读者对象**：
  - simonw指出发布公告不仅是给现有用户看的，也可能是新用户的第一次接触点，因此需要兼顾不同读者的需求。

• **标题的重要性**：
  - continuational强调发布公告的标题应传达新版本的核心和有趣之处，而非简单的版本号。

• **对营销化发布的反感**：
  - temodox明确表示不喜欢营销化的发布公告，认为纯技术性的发布说明已经足够。

争议焦点：如何在发布公告中平衡详尽的技术细节和简明的用户价值描述，以及是否应将发布说明用于营销目的。

44377666.article_content:
A release announcement showcases how the user’s experience is better today than it was yesterday. That sounds obvious, but most release announcements seem to forget that there’s a user at all.
So many release announcements just enumerate new features in a way that’s totallly divorced from how real people use the software. The announcement is essentially just a changelog with better writing.
For example, here’s a “changelog” style of announcing a new feature:
Bad: Describe what the dev team did rather than how it benefits the user
Added “repeat” button to the event menu.
Don’t just tell the user that there’s a new button. Tell the user what they can do with that button.
Good: Describe how changes benefit the user
Create recurring events automatically
🔗
In previous versions, the only way you could create weekly, monthly, or any type of recurring event was to duplicate events manually for every occurence. Duplicating events this way was tedious and error-prone.
Our latest release allows you to create recurring events automatically. Click “Options > Repeat”, and you’ll find flexible settings for repeating events on any schedule you want. You can even sync with your company’s holiday schedule to automatically skip event dates that fall on a company holiday.
Note that the example doesn’t boast about what the software can do. It tells the user what they can do with the software. It speaks directly to the user, describing what happens when “you” create events.
Release notes are not release announcements
🔗
Some software companies dump their commit history into a document, add some headings, and call that a release announcement.
Not a release announcement
That is not a release announcement. Those are release
notes
.
Release notes are fine and practical, but they’re boring.
You can publish release notes as well, but if you want users to feel excited about your newest release, give them something more interesting to read than a sterile changelog.
What to feature in a release announcement
🔗
A release announcement is a summary of the changes that will have the greatest impact on the user’s experience. It presents them in a clear, accessible way that focuses on the user.
In contrast to release notes, which aim to be exhaustive, release announcements include only the most impactful changes.
To decide which features to include in the release announcement, consider these questions:
What can the user do in the latest version that they couldn’t before?
Which workflows became easier?
Which workflows became faster?
Notice that the questions don’t include, “Which feature took the longest to complete” or “What feature contains the cleverest algorithm?”
I’ve published releases where the flagship feature was a performance improvement that only took a few hours of dev work. Implementation cost doesn’t always correlate with end-user value.
Call it “faster” not “less slow”
🔗
Some bugs are so frustrating and time-consuming to fix that you forget why you’re even fixing them in the first place. You lose sight of how the bug affects the user’s experience.
Bad: Focus on what was previously broken
Fixed a thread deadlock that froze the UI for up to two second when creating a new file.
From the user’s perspective, the new version isn’t just the same software minus a bug — it’s a tangibly better experience.
Focus on the improvement rather than the flaw. Instead of declaring the absence of a bug, celebrate how you improved the user’s experience:
Good: Focus on the improvement rather than the previous flaw
We sped up new file creation, so you can now create a new file in under 20ms, a 100x speedup from v1.2.
Briefly introduce your product
🔗
In addition to building loyalty with existing users, a release announcement should pique the interest of new, potential users.
If you publish your release announcement to the web, many of the people who read it will have never heard of your product at all.
Bad: Take it for granted that readers know your product
I’m excited to announce the 1.0 release of OpenVQ9! After 17 years of hard work, this release is a triumph for all OpenVQ9 fans, as well as the loyal developers in the OpenVQ9 ecosystem (all of whom know what OpenVQ9 is, so there’s no need to explain it here).
Early in your announcement, include a quick explanation of what your product does. If the reader isn’t familiar with your product, what’s the least they need to know to understand the rest of your announcement?
Good: Succinctly explain your product for readers unfamiliar with it
I’m excited to announce the 1.0 release of OpenVQ9, the fully open and customizable software for robot vaccum cleaners.
Don’t alienate your existing users with a 20-paragraph introduction to a product they already know. A sentence or two will provide context for new users without diluting your announcement with excessive noise for existing users.
No more “various improvements and bugfixes”
🔗
A release announcement should never include the phrase, “various improvements and

data.title: Fun with uv and PEP 723
data.author: deepakjois
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了使用 **uv** 和 **PEP 723** 元数据来简化 Python 脚本的运行和管理。  
**uv** 是一个用 Rust 编写的高效 Python 包和项目管理工具，类似于 Node/NPM 生态中的工具。其提供的 **uvx** 命令可以自动创建临时虚拟环境、安装依赖并运行 Python 工具。  
**PEP 723** 提出了一种在单文件 Python 脚本中嵌入元数据的方法，帮助启动器和 IDE 等工具处理脚本。通过结合 **uv** 和 **PEP 723**，可以轻松运行带有依赖的 Python 脚本。文章还展示了一个提取 YouTube 视频字幕的示例脚本，通过在脚本中加入 shebang 行和元数据，使其可以直接作为可执行文件运行。这种方法使 Python 脚本的执行更加便捷，类似于 Go 语言的自包含二进制文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python脚本工具和依赖管理工具（如uv）的优缺点，以及与其他语言和工具（如Go、Nix、Docker、Shell脚本）的对比

不同观点：
• ACAVJW4H认为Python脚本现在可以更轻松地运行，但Shell脚本的依赖管理和可复现性依然落后，仍依赖于手动步骤或不安全的`curl | bash`方法。虽然有Nix和Docker等工具，但它们要么复杂，要么不实用。
• epistasis对Python工具的改进表示欢迎，并提到相关博客文章的讨论，希望这些改进能得到更多关注。
• puika表示从Go转向Python用于一次性脚本和个人项目，但对Python的类型检查不满意，期待相关工具的改进。
• jkingsman高度评价uv工具的速度和易用性，虽然其文档和细节上有些粗糙，但依然愿意使用。
• satvikpendem提到Rust也有类似的单文件脚本工具，并希望更多语言采用这种模式，以便于传递小程序和脚本。
• 4dregress认为Python的依赖管理从来不是问题，尤其在大型代码库中，uv只是加快了依赖安装速度，但对整体工作流程影响不大。
• js2提到使用uv时遇到的一些小问题，尤其是在REPL中测试脚本变化时，但找到了一些解决方法。
• sambaumann对uv的速度和依赖管理表示赞赏，但认为其文档需要改进，特别是从传统工作流迁移的指导。
• rednafi坚持使用Go，因为Go可以生成独立二进制文件、依赖静态链接、标准库强大、工具链完善且稳定，对频繁变化的工具保持警惕。
• gerdesj提到Python试图兼具脚本语言和编译语言的特点，但对其安全性表示担忧，特别是`curl | bash`的不安全做法。
• tpoacher质疑整个讨论的真实性，认为像付费评论。
• pseudosavant结合ChatGPT和uv等工具，创建了许多单文件Python脚本，认为uv解决了环境管理的问题。
• kristianp提到使用conda手动管理环境的方法，虽然不如PEP 723解决方案自包含，但也是一种选择。
• divbzero希望uv能在社区中得到更广泛的应用，并提到其在不同操作系统上的安装方法。
• doctoboggan对uv是否是未来趋势表示怀疑，倾向于使用第一方内置方法，但对uv的实际效益持观望态度。

补充讨论：
• 对`curl | bash`这种不安全安装方法的普遍担忧，gerdesj特别提到需要注意安全性。
• 不同工具链（如uv、Nix、Docker、Go）在社区中的接受度和未来前景的讨论。
• 对Python类型检查和工具链的改进期望，以及与其他语言（如Go、Rust）工具链的对比。
• 对uv工具的文档和使用体验的一些具体反馈和建议。

Fun with uv and PEP 723
June 24, 2025
For the longest time, I have been frustrated with Python because I couldnât use it for one-off scripts. I had to first ensure it was running in an environment where it could find the right Python version and the dependencies installed. That is now a thing of the past.
uv
Â¶
If you are not a Pythonista (or one possibly living under a rock),
uv
is
an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
uv also provides this nifty tool called
uvx
(kinda like
npx
from the Node/NPM ecosystem for Javascript/Typescript packages) which can be used to invoke a Python tool inside a package.
uvx
takes care of creating a (cached) disposable virtual environment, setting up the right Python version and installing all the dependencies before running.
For example
$ uvx ruff --version
Installed 1 package in 5ms
ruff 0.12.0
PEP 723 - Inline script metadata
Â¶
PEP 723
is a Python Enhancement Proposal that
specifies a metadata format that can be embedded in single-file Python scripts to assist launchers, IDEs and other external tools which may need to interact with such scripts.
Here is the example directly lifted from the proposal:
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "requests<3",
#   "rich",
# ]
# ///
import
requests
from
rich.pretty
import
pprint
resp
=
requests.get(
"https://peps.python.org/api/peps.json"
)
data
=
resp.json()
pprint([(k, v[
"title"
])
for
k, v
in
data.items()][:
10
])
Using uv and PEP 723 metadata to run a Python script
Â¶
Combining uv and the PEP-723 metadata inside a Python script, we can run the script in the previous section as follows:
$ uv run pep.py
Installed 9 packages in 24ms
[

â   ('2', 'Procedure for Adding New Modules'),
â   ('3', 'Guidelines for Handling Bug Reports'),
â   ('4', 'Deprecation of Standard Modules'),
â   ('5', 'Guidelines for Language Evolution'),
â   ('6', 'Bug Fix Releases'),
â   ('7', 'Style Guide for C Code'),
â   ('8', 'Style Guide for Python Code'),
â   ('9', 'Sample Plaintext PEP Template'),
â   ('10', 'Voting Guidelines')
]

We can combine things we covered in the previous sections to create a simple executable script that can extract YouTube transcripts.
First we create a Python script with a shebang and inline metadata.

data.author: kaycebasques
data.article_summary: 本文作者首次参加YC Demo Day，认为这是一次独特的体验。YC Demo Day上的创业公司像是流水线产品，每个公司只有一分钟展示时间，风格高度一致，似乎经过统一指导。投资者可以通过专门网站查看视频和联系创业者，活动经过严格筛选，汇聚了许多有抱负的创业者。活动主题如垂直AI和Cursor for X反映了当前投资趋势。总体而言，作者认为YC Demo Day像一个商业节日，有机会接触到许多有趣的人和项目，值得参加。

不同观点：

44393418.article_content:
All Articles
Some thoughts on my first YC Demo Day
23 June 2025
#investing
#yc
This year was my first time attending YC Demo Day.
It’s a fascinating event and, really a fascinating product for investors.
Growing up in the bay area, I remember over a decade ago admiring people in YC. I was always impressed and it is a real privilege to be able to attend from the other side (as an investor).
I went not because I am a prolific investor, I went because I thought that it would be a unique experience.
The Product: Startups
This seems obvious, but the startups are the product, demo day is not a celebration of their achievement over the course of the batch, IMO it’s much more of an assembly line.
To be honest, it’s a variation
this woman on Douyin
, but applied to startups.
This woman shows a product for 3 seconds before moving onto the next one.
Rinse and repeat.
That’s YC demo day.
1 slide.
1 minute pitches.
1 speaker.
Startups are marched up there.
They get their one minute of fame and then walk off. That’s it.
All the startups are clearly coached, they communicate similarly (hand gestures, etc), every slide format is the roughly the same down to the number of bullet points.
They all conform to a particular mold.
1
The Buyer: Investors
As an investor you get access to a little website where you can view the videos. You can also get intro’d to the startup via email or message them directly.
You setup your profile in there and so you’ve got to appear legitimate as well.
what you get
The program heavily filters these batches for high-agency people and folks who want to get after it.
The program has already vetted these people as those willing to sacrifice and make things happen, including dropouts leaving successful jobs. It’s an admirable collection of people.
The base terms for investments
2 on 20 is the standard for startups coming out of YC. It seems to me that this is the benchmark for what the teams are going for and you can get a sense for excitement based on how filled out that allocation is.
Notable Themes
Vertical AI was all over the place.
Cursor for X was also prevalent.
This is more of a reflection on the event itself, so I won’t go into too much detail but it’s an interesting pulse of not only what people want to build but also what people want to invest in.
The community
I met some pretty amazing folks. Exited founders, internet friends. It’s a pretty astonishing collection and community and there’s quite a bit of value there.
It honestly felt a bit more like a business festival, the networking was bumping and there’s real momentum there. I met a lot of interesting people, people that I wouldn’t have gotten exposure to otherwise.
Conclusions
It was a great event. I enjoyed it, if you have the opportunity, I’d recommend going. It’s a spectacle!
Footnotes
Note, I don’t mean this negatively. It’s just they’ve got a format that works, that is the standard, and you’ve got to deliver against that.

data.title: A lumberjack created more than 200 sculptures in Wisconsin's Northwoods
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 退休伐木工弗雷德·史密斯在20世纪40年代末至60年代中期，于威斯康星州创建了超过200座真人大小的混凝土雕塑，这些雕塑展现了当地文化、民间传说以及美国历史和爱国主义象征。史密斯的作品核心为木结构，外包水泥、镶嵌碎玻璃等物品，如今保存在威斯康星混凝土公园。由于长期暴露于自然环境中，雕塑需要持续维护，保护员使用环氧树脂、硅胶等材料修复破损和不稳，并加固生锈的支撑结构。公园免费开放，但鼓励捐款以支持保护工作。

44393160.article_content:
Over the years, a conservator replaced the headgear on deer with real antlers and the originals mounted on moose with synthetic alternatives.
Carol M. Highsmith/Buyenlarge/Getty Images
During Fred Smith’s golden years, art inexplicably began to pour out of him. The retired lumberjack loved to work with his hands, think with his hands, speak with his hands—and one day, like magic, he began to create with his hands.
Bent over by age and arthritis, the Phillips, Wisconsin, resident continued to build life-size and larger-than-life concrete sculptures—over 200 in all—from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s, blending local culture and lore with the wider world and the great beyond.
Smith’s homestead farm soon filled with images from his life and imagination as he depicted everything from everyday folks to folk heroes, as well as symbols of American history, patriotism and spirituality.
The sculptures are loosely organized by theme. Even so, the panorama of animals, humans and objects all seem to mix and mingle in the same landscape, leading to plenty of intriguing juxtapositions. Picture everything from Sacagawea and the Statue of Liberty to a
musky
so massive it’s pulled by a team of horses.
When asked about his monuments, Smith, who died in 1976 at 89 years old, would simply respond with laughter. “Nobody knows why I made them,”
he said
. “Not even me.”
Retired lumberjack Fred Smith built more than 200 sculptures on his farm from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s.
Wisconsin Concrete Park
Unable to read or write, he taught himself to form these sculptures using wooden structures at their core wrapped in mink or barbed wire, covered in layers of cement, and adorned with broken glass and other found objects.
Today, his eclectic display lives on at the
Wisconsin Concrete Park
, an outdoor sculpture garden situated within a
16-acre setting
in the state’s sparsely populated Northwoods region, where the trees outnumber the people.
What shines through in Smith’s work—nearly half a century after his departure—is a profound reverence for nature and for the many ordinary and extraordinary people, places and events explored throughout his art.
Preservation tools and techniques
Surviving the area’s elements, particularly the long and frigid winters, is easier said than done, though. What visitors may overlook is the painstaking upkeep that goes into these folk art statues that are exposed to Mother Nature’s whims and Father Time’s unrelenting wear and tear.
This past year, for example, a tree branch took Paul Bunyan’s head off, injured his arm and walloped one of his wolfhounds in one fell swoop, says Ann Grzywnowicz, operations manager of the
Friends of Fred Smith
, a nonprofit formed to preserve the park and develop it into an educational and cultural facility.
Restoring the legendary lumberjack to his former glory will be one of the biggest and most significant projects awaiting Ben Caguioa, a sculpture conservator based in Chicago, when he returns this summer to tackle the most recent round of destruction caused by wind, water and winter.
Need to know: How to visit the Wisconsin Concrete Park
The Wisconsin Concrete Park is located just south of Phillips, in Price County, Wisconsin.
The park is open to the public year-round during daylight hours. No admission is required, but donations are encouraged, as the funds go toward preservation work.
His toolbox includes a range of materials—such as marine epoxies, fumed silica and elastomeric caulking—meant to restore structural integrity and aesthetic appeal. This undertaking involves repairing breaks, fixing instabilities, strengthening sculptures or leveling those that have begun to tilt.
Along the way, Caguioa has replaced antlers, reinforced legs and re-leveled the big fish. He has also worked extensively on the lumberjacks near the park entrance, one of which completely collapsed and had to be rebuilt from the ground up.
Many of these sculptures were assembled around wooden two-by-fours, and these box frames—especially within the human figures—gradually decay. The armature that runs up through the legs is made of galvanized pipe that rusts out.
Since there are only two points of contact with the ground, the statues eventually begin to wobble. To reinforce ankles, Caguioa inserts stainless steel rods within the galvanized pipe or replaces that pipe with a steel rod of equivalent thickness.
On breaks and cracks, the conservator uses marine epoxies to establish a solid connection. “I’ll inject that into the cracks using a syringe,” Caguioa says. When he needs to fill a larger gap, he thickens the epoxy with fumed silica to achieve a consistency that resembles a viscous ointment. From there, Caguioa disguises the fractures using elastomeric caulking dusted with sand to replicate the appearance of the original concrete.
If the sculpture spans two or more bases or if the original base is cracked, he’ll use flexible joints to compensate for the movement, much like the
expansion join

data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发行业的职业倦怠、行业变化以及应对策略

不同观点：
• [tptacek] 认为每隔7-8年就会产生一次职业倦怠，并指出在这种情绪下做出的决定往往是不理智的。他以自身经验说明这种感觉是周期性的，建议不要在此时做出重大决定。

• [_wire_] 对企业持批判态度，认为企业并不是人道机构，而是以利益为重，不惜牺牲有技能和责任感的员工。他还指出，所谓的智能和进步只是特权阶层的夸张说法，当公司福利枯竭时，这个阶层也会随之消亡。

• [tonestonestones] 认为软件开发正走向自动化，这是不可避免的自然演变。虽然不幸，但也是一种机会，可以去做更有趣的事情。他还提到管理者需要被替换，除非他们能比技术人员看得更远。

• [protocolture] 表达了对当前工作环境的不满，指出雇主和客户都在维持过时的做法，而不愿投资于技术更新，这让他们付出了更高的成本。

• [m0llusk] 认为软件工程师有能力创建自己的公司，不必局限于行业内的工作，这可能是摆脱当前困境的一种途径。

• [AdamH12113] 建议离开硅谷，去小公司工作，这些公司虽然无法提供高薪，但工作可能更有意义，能带来不同的满足感。

• [colechristensen] 认为倦怠和负面情绪是可以理解的，但建议寻求专业帮助，通过积极的方式来处理这些情绪，找到新的方向，而不是让愤怒伤害自己。

• [jaronilan] 分享了一篇幽默文章，暗示当前招聘市场的困境，间接支持了对行业现状的批评。

• [itsthecourier] 指出LLMs（大型语言模型）的应用将大大减少对人力的需求，尤其是对高级工程师的需求，这给行业带来了更大压力，并提到自2021年以来行业的收缩。

• [gedy] 提醒大家当前是市场低谷，公司会变得非常挑剔，自学成才的人在此时可能不占优势。他还指出，软件行业过去几十年过得很轻松，其他行业的情况可能更糟。

• [regflid] 对某些评论中的傲慢和性别歧视态度提出批评，指出这种态度可能是导致个人职业困境的原因之一。

• [crsv] 持强硬态度，认为世界本就是残酷的，个人不应期待被给予任何东西，而应自强不息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是对企业和管理者的不满情绪，一些人如[_wire_]和[protocolture]对企业持强烈批判态度，而[regflid]则认为这种批判可能是个人问题导致的。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是LLMs和自动化对行业的冲击，[tonestonestones]和[itsthecourier]都提到了自动化对就业市场的负面影响。
• 职业倦怠和应对策略也是一个重要讨论点，[colechristensen]建议通过积极的方式处理情绪，而[AdamH12113]则提出通过地理位置的改变来寻找新的机会。

data.title: Collections: Nitpicking Gladiator's Iconic Opening Battle, Part I
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 文章分析了电影《角斗士》(2000)开场战斗场景的历史准确性，指出该场景尽管视觉上看似真实，实际上充满了历史错误。文章提到，虽然这场战斗场景在公众想象中塑造了对罗马军队的认知，但其细节如军队组成、战术、武器和胜利策略等均不符历史事实。特别指出，场景中罗马军队过于依赖骑兵和弓箭手，而这并不符合当时罗马军队的战斗方式。此外，文章还以主角“Maximus Decimus Meridius”的名字为例，说明其看似像罗马名字，实则完全不符罗马命名 conventions。文章强调，该场景营造了一种“貌似真实”的效果，但并非真正的历史再现，提醒观众不应被表面的视觉细节所误导。文章作者表明，尽管《角斗士》在历史细节上有诸多错误，但仍可以欣赏这部电影，只需认识到其历史不准确性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对导演Ridley Scott历史题材电影中历史准确性的不同看法

不同观点：
• Shorel的观点：Shorel认为Ridley Scott有创作自由，但历史学家也有权指出与历史不符的地方。这并不是吹毛求疵，而是传达真实的历史科学知识，这与电影本身同样重要，甚至更重要。Shorel强调，不是所有事情都是为了赚最多的钱，有时遗产在于根据最好的研究准确叙述事件。

• ggm的观点：ggm认为Ridley Scott知道自己并不总是历史准确的，他对某些事情在意，而对其他事情则不在意。Scott更关注视觉上的美感和历史上的“可接受”框架。ggm指出，Scott可能会误用一些历史细节，如武器和装甲，但不会做过于离谱的事情，如给Russel Crowe一支射线枪。ggm还提到，Scott不喜欢被吹毛求疵，并认为Scott的电影《The Duellists》在细节上非常出色。

• Rebelgecko的观点：Rebelgecko关注电影中的服装错误，特别是战后有人穿着牛仔裤走动，认为这是最明显的错误。

补充讨论：
• staplung的观点：staplung提出比较Ridley Scott的战场场景和电视剧《Rome》第一季第一集中的场景，尽管后者预算较低且场景较短。这暗示了对不同作品中历史场景表现的比较兴趣。

争议焦点：Ridley Scott历史题材电影中的历史准确性以及历史学家和电影创作者之间的不同优先级。Shorel和ggm之间的讨论反映了创作者艺术自由与历史准确性之间的张力。Rebelgecko的具体例子进一步强调了观众对细节错误的关注。

44360630.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
June 6, 2025
June 6, 2025
33 Minutes
This week, we’re going to take a close look at arguably the most famous and recognizable Roman battle sequence in film: the iconic opening battle from
Gladiator
(2000).
1
Despite being a relatively short sequence (about ten minutes), there’s actually enough to talk about here that we’re going to split it over two weeks, talking about the setup – the battlefield, army composition, equipment and battle plan – this week and then the actual conduct of the battle next week.
The iconic opening battle, set in the Marcomannic Wars (166-180) during the reign of Marcus Aurelius (r. 161-180)
dominates
the pop-cultural reference points for the Roman army in battle and you can see its heavy influence in things like how the
Total War
series presents Roman armies (particularly in trailers and other promotional material).  Students and enthusiasts alike will often cite this sequence as the thing which sparked their interest in the Roman army.  It is hard to overstate how
pervasive
its influence is in the public imagination of what the Roman army, particularly of the imperial period, was like, especially as its style is imitated by later pop culture works.
Which is why it is so unfortunate that it is such a deceptive historical mess
. This sequence
in particular
is a banner example of what I’ve termed elsewhere the ‘
perils of historical verisimilitude
,’ the habit of historically based popular-culture works including what we might think of as fake
signifiers
of research, things that
seem
historically grounded rather than
being
historically grounded, as a way to cheaply cash in on the cachet that an actually grounded representation gets a work.
Gladiator
actually provides a perfect metaphor for this: its main character’s name.  Russell Crowe proudly informs us he is, “Maximus Decimus Meridius,” a name that certainly
sounds
suitably Roman, picking up the three-part name with that standard second declension -us ending.  It
sounds
like it could be a real name – if you didn’t know Latin you would probably
assume
that it could be a real Roman name.  But,
as we’ve noted
,
it isn’t a Roman name
and in fact
gets nearly all of the Roman naming conventions wrong
: Roman names are ordered as praenomen, nomen and cognomen, with the nomen indicating one’s
gens
(‘clan’ more or less) and the praenomen selected from just a couple dozen common personal names.  Decimus is one of those two-dozen common praenomina (which also means it is never going to show up as the name of a
gens
), so it ought to go first as it is actually his personal name.  Meanwhile Maximus (‘the greatest’) is very much
not
one of those roughly two-dozen praenomina, instead being always cognomen (essentially a nickname).  Finally Meridius isn’t a Latin word at all (so it can’t be a praenomen personal name nor a cognomen nickname),
2
meaning it has to be the nomen (referencing a fictive
gens Meridia
).
Every part of his name is wrong
and it
should
read Decimus Meridius Maximus.
It
sounds just right enough
to fool your average viewer, while
being entirely wrong
.  It is ‘truthy’ rather than true – verisimilitudinous (
like
truth), rather than veristic (realistic, true).
In the case of
Gladiator
‘s opening battle scene,
the attention is on creating verisimilitude
(without fidelity, as we’ll see)
in the
visual
elements of the sequence and
only
the visual elements
.  The
visual
representation of a Roman army – the equipment in particular – is heavily based on the Column of Trajan (including replicating the Column’s own deceptions) and since that is the one thing a viewer can easily
check
, that verisimilitude leads a lot of viewers to conclude that the entire sequence is much more historically grounded than it is.  They take their cues from the one thing they can judge – ‘do these fellows wear that strange armor I saw on that picture of a Roman column?’ – and assume everything is about as well researched, when in fact none of it is.
Instead, apart from the equipment – which has its own deep flaws – this is a sequence that bears almost no resemblance to the way Roman armies fought and expected to win their battles.  The Roman army in this sequence has the wrong composition, is deployed incorrectly, uses the wrong tactics, has the wrong theory of victory and employs the wrong weapons and then employs them incorrectly.  Perhaps most importantly the sequence suggests an oddly cavalry-and-archer focused Roman army which is simply not how the Romans in this period expected to win their battles.
Now I want to be clear here that this isn’t a
review
of the film
Gladiator
(2000) or my opinion in general on the film.  To be honest,
unlike
the
recent
sequel
, I enjoy
Gladiator
even though it is historical gibberish.  So I am not telling you that you aren’t ‘allowed’ to like
Gladiator
, but rather simply that, despite appearances, it is historical gibberish, particularly this opening scene, which I often find folks who are aw

data.title: Apple Research unearthed forgotten AI technique and using it to generate images
data.author: celias
data.article_summary:
苹果公司通过两篇新论文重新挖掘了一种被遗忘的AI技术——归一化流（Normalizing Flows），并用于图像生成。与目前主流的扩散模型和自回归模型不同，归一化流模型通过学习将真实数据转换为结构化噪声并反向生成新样本。其优势在于能精确计算生成图像的概率，适用于对结果概率要求高的任务。

第一篇论文介绍的TarFlow模型引入了Transformer块，将图像分割成小块进行自回归生成，避免了图像压缩成固定词汇导致的质量损失。第二篇论文的STARFlow模型进一步改进，在压缩后的潜在空间中生成图像，再通过解码器恢复到高分辨率，提升了生成效率和图像质量。

与OpenAI的GPT-4o通过序列化标记生成图像不同，苹果的模型直接生成像素值，更适合移动设备，展现了其在便携设备上的潜力。

主要讨论点：苹果公司在人工智能（AI）领域中的定位及其技术选择，特别是关于图像生成技术和本地计算的优势。

不同观点：
• **[bitpush]** 认为苹果相关媒体过度渲染苹果在AI竞赛中的地位，实际上苹果只是发布了早在2021年就开始研究的技术，标题有误导之嫌。他指出，苹果的技术并非独特，而是基于四年前的技术。

• **[kelseyfrog]** 同意2021年的技术可能在AI领域中被遗忘，但认为这并不影响其价值。他引用了NVAE论文，认为四年的时间足以让一些技术被遗忘。

• **[imoverclocked]** 赞赏苹果在本地设备上实现复杂计算的能力，认为这种做法增加了产品的整体价值和用户体验，使用户能够完全掌握产品。

• **[b0a04gl]** 强调使用flow模型不仅因为其大小合适，还因为其完全可逆和确定性的特点。这可以确保在不同设备和芯片上获得一致的输出，有利于缓存、测试和用户信任，符合苹果一贯的确定性DNA。

• **[rfv6723]** 指出苹果AI团队专注于小型设备模型，这与广泛接受的“大规模模型更有效”的观点（ bitter lesson ）相悖。他们认为长期来看，这种策略的结果值得观察。

补充讨论：
• **[MBCook]** 对flow模型在相同硬件上的速度表现提出疑问，想了解其与常见方法的性能对比。

• **[nextaccountic]** 对文章的真实性提出质疑，希望有类似于“举报”的按钮来标记疑似AI生成的内容，特别是某些部分看起来像是AI编写。

• **[celias]** 和 **[tiahura]** 提供了相关论文和GitHub链接，为讨论提供了技术参考和资源支持。

争议焦点：苹果是否在AI竞赛中具有独特地位，及其选择的小型设备模型策略的长期有效性。

44358535.article_content:
Apple Research
Apple Research just unearthed a forgotten AI technique and is using it to generate images
Marcus Mendes
| Jun 23 2025 - 8:59 am PT
4 Comments
Today, most generative image models basically fall into two main categories: diffusion models, like Stable Diffusion, or autoregressive models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4o. But Apple just released two papers that show how there might be room for a third, forgotten technique: Normalizing Flows. And with a dash of Transformers on top, they might be more capable than previously thought.
First things first: What are Normalizing Flows?
Normalizing Flows (NFs) are a type of AI model that works by learning how to mathematically transform real-world data (like images) into structured noise, and then reverse that process to generate new samples.
The big advantage is that they can calculate the exact likelihood of each image they generate, a property that diffusion models can’t do. This makes flows especially appealing for tasks where understanding the probability of an outcome really matters.
But there’s a reason most people haven’t heard much about them lately: Early flow-based models produced images that looked blurry or lacked the detail and diversity offered by diffusion and transformer-based systems.
Study #1: TarFlow
In the paper “
Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
”, Apple introduces a new model called TarFlow, short for Transformer AutoRegressive Flow.
At its core, TarFlow replaces the old, handcrafted layers used in previous flow models with Transformer blocks. Basically, it splits images into small patches, and generates them in blocks, with each block predicted based on all the ones that came before. That’s what’s called autoregressive, which is the same underlying method that OpenAI currently uses for image generation.
Images of various resolutions generated by TarFlow models. From left to right, top to bottom: 256×256 images on AFHQ, 128×128 and 64×64 images on ImageNet. Source:
Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
The key difference is that while OpenAI generates discrete tokens, treating images like long sequences of text-like symbols, Apple’s TarFlow generates pixel values directly, without tokenizing the image first. It’s a small, but significant difference because it lets Apple avoid the quality loss and rigidity that often come with compressing images into a fixed vocabulary of tokens.
Still, there were limitations, especially when it came to scaling up to larger, high-res images. And that’s where the second study comes in.
Study #2: STARFlow
In the paper “
STARFlow: Scaling Latent Normalizing Flows for High-resolution Image Synthesis
”, Apple builds directly on TarFlow and presents STARFlow (Scalable Transformer AutoRegressive Flow), with key upgrades.
The biggest change: STARFlow no longer generates images directly in pixel space. Instead, it basically works on a compressed version of the image, and then hands things off to a decoder that upsamples everything back to full resolution at the final step.
Random samples of STARFlow on ImageNet 256 ×256 and 512 ×512. Source:
STARFlow: Scaling Latent Normalizing Flows for High-resolution Image Synthesis
This shift to what is called latent space means STARFlow doesn’t need to predict millions of pixels directly. It can focus on the broader image structure first, leaving fine texture detail to the decoder.
Apple also reworked how the model handles text prompts. Instead of building a separate text encoder, STARFlow can plug in existing language models (like Google’s small language model Gemma, which in theory could run on-device) to handle language understanding when the user prompts the model to create the image. This keeps the image generation side of the model focused on refining visual details.
How STARFlow compares with OpenAI’s 4o image generator
While Apple is rethinking flows, OpenAI has also recently moved beyond diffusion with its GPT-4o model. But their approach is fundamentally different.
GPT-4o treats images as sequences of discrete tokens, much like words in a sentence. When you ask ChatGPT to generate an image, the model predicts one image token at a time, building the picture piece by piece. This gives OpenAI enormous flexibility: the same model can generate text, images, and audio within a single, unified token stream.
The tradeoff? Token-by-token generation can be slow, especially for large or high-resolution images. And it’s extremely computationally expensive. But since GPT-4o runs entirely in the cloud, OpenAI isn’t as constrained by latency or power use.
In short: both Apple and OpenAI are moving beyond diffusion, but while OpenAI is building for its data centers, Apple is clearly building for our pockets.

44358535.article_summary:
苹果公司通过两篇新论文重新挖掘了一种被遗忘的AI技术——归一化流（Normalizing Flows），并用于图像生成。与目前主流的扩散模型和自回归模型不同，归一化流模型通过学习将真实数据转换为结构化噪声并反向生成新样本。其优势在于能精确计算生成图像的概率，适用于对结果概率要求高的任务。

第一篇论文介绍的TarFlow模型引入了Transformer块，将图像分割成小块进行自回归生成，避免了图像压缩成固定词汇导致的质量损失。第二篇论文的STARFlow模型进一步改进，在压缩后的潜在空间中生成图像，再通过解码器恢复到高分辨率，提升了生成效率和图像质量。

与OpenAI的GPT-4o通过序列化标记生成图像不同，苹果的模型直接生成像素值，更适合移动设备，展现了其在便携设备上的潜力。

data.title: Define policy forbidding use of AI code generators
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: QEMU项目当前政策拒绝接受包含或衍生自AI生成内容（如ChatGPT、Copilot、Llama等工具）的贡献。这是因为AI生成内容的版权和许可状态不明确，存在法律风险。QEMU贡献者需根据开发者原产地证书（DCO）规则，确保对提交内容的版权和许可有完全理解。由于AI工具的输出无法满足DCO要求，项目不允许在提交的补丁中使用这些工具生成的内容。不过，AI工具在研究API、算法、静态分析或调试等非提交相关用途上仍可使用。此政策可能随AI工具和法律情况成熟而调整，但目前需逐案申请例外并证明输出内容的版权和许可状态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成代码对开源和自由软件的影响，尤其是在版权和法律问题、代码质量审查、项目管理等方面的挑战。

不同观点：
• **benlivengood**：认为开源和自由软件特别容易受到AI生成代码的版权问题影响。如果AI生成的代码被判定为侵权或公共领域，项目可能会陷入法律诉讼，且开源项目通常没有足够资金应对。此外，AI生成的代码经过人类修改后是否仍属于侵权衍生作品存在不确定性。如果AI生成代码被视为公共领域，则开源许可的约束力会削弱。

• **JonChesterfield**：对AI生成代码持批评态度，认为不应接受开发者自己都不理解的代码，也不愿意合并这种代码。这种立场比LLVM项目的政策更加严格。

• **acedTrex**：指出AI生成代码打破了传统上通过隐藏能力标记判断贡献质量的方式。AI生成的代码虽然看起来专业，但缺乏实际经验支撑，可能对经验丰富的开发者造成困扰。未来，可能需要更多依赖社交证明等方式来评估贡献者。

• **ants_everywhere**：认为RedHat等大公司关注AI生成代码的风险，主要是因为AI可能输出属于其他项目的代码，尤其是涉及闭源和可能引发诉讼的代码。

• **Havoc**：质疑一些项目反对AI生成代码的动机，认为可能不仅仅是因为法律问题，而是因为对低质量AI提交感到厌烦。

• **saurik**：指出QEMU项目由于其仿真器性质，已经面临较大的法律 scrutiny，因此需要比其他项目更加保守地对待AI生成代码，以避免增加法律风险。

• **hughw**：希望能够在使用LLM作为IDE的自动补全工具和生成实质性代码之间做出区分。虽然这是一个灰色地带，但希望使用AI工具节省劳动力的同时，不涉及版权问题。

• **bgwalter**：认为反对AI生成代码的政策可能只是为了在使用AI生成代码时有合理的否认权，实际上这些政策可能根本无法执行。

• **Aeolun**：认为执行反对AI生成代码的政策几乎不可能，因为现代编辑器普遍提供AI辅助代码提示，且无法区分这些提示和手动输入的代码。

• **daeken**：分享了自己使用Claude Code工具调试代码的经验，发现AI工具在复杂项目中目前还不能提供实际价值，虽然未来可能有潜力。

• **flerchin**：认为使用AI生成代码的贡献者需要对其代码负责，并深入理解代码，以应对审查中的质疑。

• **wyldfire**：认为除了拒绝AI生成代码外，还可以指定某些部分允许使用AI生成内容，并设立防护措施。

• **tqwhite**：认为担心AI生成代码是合理的，但政策不应禁止使用AI，而是确保不留下使用痕迹。同时，AI生成的程序未来可能会像从前一样具有版权。

• **zoobab**：暗示RedHat等大公司现在控制了QEMU项目，可能影响项目的独立性。

• **randomNumber7**：认为AI生成代码仍然比手动编写快，开发者可以阅读和检查AI生成的代码以确保其符合需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成代码的版权归属和质量问题，以及如何在开源项目中有效管理AI生成代码的使用。
• 不同项目对AI生成代码的态度和政策有所不同，部分项目采取严格禁止的立场，而其他项目可能允许在特定条件下使用。
• 实际操作中，如何区分和监管AI生成代码的使用仍然是一个复杂且未完全解决的问题。

data.title: Microsoft is moving antivirus providers out of the Windows kernel
data.author: mrcsharp
data.article_summary: 微软计划对Windows进行更改，以防止类似CrowdStrike事件的再次发生。去年，CrowdStrike的一次错误更新导致全球850万台Windows设备崩溃，促使微软采取行动。微软将与CrowdStrike、Bitdefender、ESET等安全厂商合作，将反病毒和终端检测响应（EDR）应用移出Windows内核。微软强调，他们不是单方面制定规则，而是与行业伙伴共同设计平台。虽然这一变化不会立即解决所有内核驱动问题，但将首先从反病毒和EDR开始。微软还计划发布“快速机器恢复”功能，并 redesign 蓝屏死机（BSOD）为黑屏。微软希望通过这些改变提高系统安全性和可靠性。

News
Microsoft is moving antivirus providers out of the Windows kernel
Microsoft is ready to test Windows changes to prevent another CrowdStrike incident.
Microsoft is ready to test Windows changes to prevent another CrowdStrike incident.
by
Tom Warren
Jun 26, 2025, 4:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: The Verge
Tom Warren
is a senior editor and author of
Notepad
, who has been covering all things Microsoft, PC, and tech for over 20 years.
It’s been nearly a year since a faulty CrowdStrike update
took down 8.5 million
Windows-based machines around the world, and Microsoft wants to ensure such a problem never happens again. After
holding a summit
with security vendors last year, Microsoft is poised to release a private preview of Windows changes that will move antivirus (AV) and endpoint detection and response (EDR) apps out of the Windows kernel.
The new Windows endpoint security platform is being built in cooperation with CrowdStrike, Bitdefender, ESET, Trend Micro, and many other security vendors. “We’ve had dozens of partners supply papers to us, some of them hundreds of pages long, on how they’d like it to be designed and what the requirements are,” explains David Weston, vice president of enterprise and OS security at Microsoft, in an interview with
The Verge
. “I’ve been really pleased with this. It’s an industry of competitors but everyone has stepped up and said we’ve got to build a platform that all of us work on.”
Microsoft is keen to stress that it’s not setting the rules and expecting everyone to immediately follow them, but instead build the rules together. “We’re not here to tell them how the API should work, we’re here to listen and provide the security and reliability,” Weston says. “I think if we’d gone out that some of our competitors and said, ‘Here it is, take it or leave it,’ that would really be a challenge.”
For decades, Microsoft has built Windows in a way that has allowed developers to deliver security software that’s deeply rooted into Windows, running at the kernel level of Windows — the core part of an operating system that has unrestricted access to system memory and hardware. The faulty CrowdStrike update last year highlighted just how easy it is for a kernel-level driver to go wrong and take down a machine, resulting in a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD).
Microsoft now has some of its most knowledgeable Windows engineers working on these security changes. “We’ve had key developers on this, some of the kernel architects of Windows and people that don’t even traditionally work in security,” Weston says. “It’s really the biggest brains of core Windows being involved and collaborating with CrowdStrike, ESET, and all those folks.”
The private preview will give security vendors a chance to request changes. Weston says he expects a few iterations until it’s ready for vendors to make the switch. It’s also not going to solve every single kernel-level driver instance straight away. “Our goal is to start with AV and EDR, but there will likely be kernel drivers for some period as we move on to the next set of use cases.”
Another big area of Windows that uses kernel-level drivers is anti-cheating engines for games. Microsoft has been speaking with game developers about how to reduce the amount of kernel usage, but it’s a more complicated use case as cheaters often have to purposefully tamper with their machine to disable protections and get cheating engines running.
“A lot of [game developers] would love to not have to maintain kernel stuff, and they are very interested in how they do that,” Weston says. “We’ve been talking about the requirements there, and I think we’ll have more to say on that in the near future.”
Riot Games told me last year
that it’s willing to follow potential Windows security changes and “recede from the kernel space.”
While it’s going to take Microsoft and security vendors some time to work through these Windows changes, Microsoft is confident that it will see good adoption rates because its customers are asking for changes in the wake of the CrowdStrike incident.
Microsoft is also getting ready to release a Windows update later this summer that will include a new
Quick Machine Recovery
feature, which is designed to quickly restore machines that can’t boot. It prompts a device to enter the Windows Recovery Environment, where the machine can access the network and provide Microsoft with diagnostic information. “We basically built the thing we’d love to have had for the incident last year,” Weston says.
The sight of a Blue Screen of Death will also be a thing of the past, too. Microsoft is now officially redesigning its BSOD so that it’s black and not blue.
More on that big change here
.

data.title: -2000 Lines of code (2004)
data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了1982年Lisa软件团队试图通过每周编写的代码行数来衡量工程师的进度。然而，核心工程师比尔·阿特金森认为这种方法不合理，他致力于编写简洁高效的代码，而不是追求代码数量。在优化Quickdraw区域计算功能时，他重写了代码，使速度提高了六倍，并减少了2000行代码。当被要求填写管理表格时，他幽默地在代码行数栏填上了“-2000”。几周后，管理层不再要求他填写这份表格。故事表明，单纯以代码行数衡量编程效率是不可取的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码删除和简化的重要性，以及代码量是否能作为衡量开发者效率的有效指标。

不同观点：
• **代码删除是重要且有益的**：
  - bironran分享了通过删除60K行代码并替换为更轻量的逻辑，成功优化了系统性能的经历，认为减少代码量是算法上的胜利。
  - jfengel提到在大学期间删除大量冗余代码的经历，强调删除不必要代码对系统稳定性的重要性。
  - dml2135提到在工作中移除C#和WinRT互操作支持的经历，认为这是必要的“破坏性变更”。
  - impostervt分享了通过重构和重写，将250K行代码减少到17K行，极大地简化了项目。

• **代码量不能作为衡量开发质量的唯一标准**：
  - dang分享了多个关于“2000行代码”讨论的链接，表明代码量不能简单地用来评估代码质量。
  - jaydeegee提到在运维中使用的“工单处理量”指标，指出这种统计可能会被误导，因不同人的工作方式不同。
  - tregoning指出仍有公司使用代码行数作为绩效指标，质疑这种做法的合理性。

• **代码简化和重构的价值**：
  - dang强调了回顾和重温经典讨论的价值，认为这有助于新手开发者学习。
  - mapmeld提到在年度绩效评审前发现自己净减少了代码量，认为这是对项目有积极贡献的。
  - rottc0dd通过学习与实践，优化了项目代码结构，强调了数据抽象和简化逻辑的重要性。

• **代码量作为激励手段的争议**：
  - abraxas引用Dilbert漫画，讽刺通过修复bug来获取奖励的做法，暗示这种激励可能导致不良行为。
  - justtinker分享了通过简化代码减少97%代码量的经历，但因代码风格不同而遭遇团队成员的抵制。

补充讨论：
- **文化与习惯**：dml2135提到在共享艺术空间中的“清理”文化，并将其应用于开发环境，强调清理无用代码是开发的一部分。
- **历史与经验**：vodou分享了关于开发团队使用错误指标的经历，强调有害的度量方式会对团队成员造成负面影响。
- **技术与方法**：rottc0dd通过学习hashmap实现来优化项目，表明不断学习和应用新方法对代码简化的重要性。

44381252.article_content: Home Â |Â About Folklore | Quotes The Original Macintosh: Â Â Â 38 of 125Â -2000 Lines Of Code Author: Andy Hertzfeld Date: February 1982 Characters: Bill Atkinson Topics: Software Design, Management, Lisa Summary: It's hard to measure progress by lines of code In early 1982, the Lisa software team was trying to buckle down for the big push to ship the software within the next six months. Some of the managers decided that it would be a good idea to track the progress of each individual engineer in terms of the amount of code that they wrote from week to week. They devised a form that each engineer was required to submit every Friday, which included a field for the number of lines of code that were written that week. Bill Atkinson, the author of Quickdraw and the main user interface designer, who was by far the most important Lisa implementer, thought that lines of code was a silly measure of software productivity. He thought his goal was to write as small and fast a program as possible, and that the lines of code metric only encouraged writing sloppy, bloated, broken code. He recently was working on optimizing Quickdraw's region calculation machinery, and had completely rewritten the region engine using a simpler, more general algorithm which, after some tweaking, made region operations almost six times faster. As a by-product, the rewrite also saved around 2,000 lines of code. He was just putting the finishing touches on the optimization when it was time to fill out the management form for the first time. When he got to the lines of code part, he thought about it for a second, and then wrote in the number: -2000. I'm not sure how the managers reacted to that, but I do know that after a couple more weeks, they stopped asking Bill to fill out the form, and he gladly complied. data.title: How the next financial crisis starts. The climate shocks that trigger turmoil
data.author: Traces
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国每年花费近1万亿美元用于气候灾害的损失

不同观点：
• 观点一：政府应加大对可再生能源和绿色技术的投资，以减少未来在气候灾害上的支出。支持这一观点的网友指出，持续依赖化石燃料会进一步加剧气候变化，导致未来更多的经济损失。他们认为，现在投资绿色技术虽然昂贵，但长远来看可以减少灾害带来的巨额开支。

• 观点二：有人质疑当前政府在应对气候变化上的效率，认为大量资金被浪费在无效的项目上，且存在腐败和资金管理不善的问题。他们认为，即使投入大量资金，如果无法有效利用，问题仍然得不到解决。有网友举例提到，过去一些环保项目由于执行不力而失败，浪费了纳税人的钱。

• 观点三：部分人持悲观态度，认为无论投入多少资金，气候变化已经不可逆转，未来的灾害损失难以避免。他们认为，与其一味投入资金试图阻止气候变化，不如将部分资金用于建设更具弹性的基础设施，帮助社区更好地应对灾害。有网友建议投资建设防洪堤、抗震建筑等设施，以减少灾害带来的实际损失。

• 观点四：有人提出私人企业也应承担更多责任，特别是在推动绿色技术创新和减少碳排放方面。他们认为，政府不应独自承担应对气候变化的全部责任，企业应通过技术创新和可持续发展实践来减少环境影响。有网友提到，大公司尤其是化石燃料企业应为气候变化负更多责任，并应出资进行环境修复。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于资金的使用效率和优先级问题。一部分人认为政府应优先投资于减缓气候变化的项目，另一部分人则认为应优先建设应对灾害的基础设施。还有人提到，不同地区在气候变化中的责任和应对能力不同，联邦政府应更公平地分配资金，帮助受灾严重但财政能力较弱的地区。

• 讨论中有人提到国际合作的重要性，认为美国应在气候变化问题上与其他国家合作，尤其是与那些受气候变化影响严重的国家。他们认为，气候变化是一个全球性问题，单靠一个国家的投入无法根本解决问题。

data.title: Games run faster on SteamOS than Windows 11, Ars testing finds
data.author: _JamesA_
data.article_summary: Ars Technica的测试显示，在Lenovo Legion Go S上，SteamOS 3.7的游戏帧率表现普遍优于Windows 11，这在大多数高画质游戏中尤为明显。测试的五款游戏中，有四款在SteamOS上表现出更高的帧率，仅《Borderlands 3》在Windows上略胜一筹。特别是在低画质设置下，操作系统的选择可能决定游戏是否流畅运行。尽管Windows需要通过额外安装Asus提供的非官方驱动才能接近SteamOS的性能，但在多数情况下，Windows的帧率仍比SteamOS低8%到36%。SteamOS通过Proton翻译层实现的高效兼容性，使其在游戏性能上超越了传统Windows系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux与Windows在游戏性能和体验上的比较

不同观点：
• **Haswell**：根据个人经验，Linux通过Proton和Wayland的组合在Steam上的性能表现优于Windows。特别提到从X11切换到Wayland时帧率有明显提升，且游戏帧率一致性更好。但也指出游戏启动时间可能较长。
• **Jekwoooooe**：强调Linux gaming目前的主要问题在于反作弊支持不足，许多游戏因为缺乏反作弊支持而无法在Linux上运行。期待未来能完全转向Linux。
• **Sitkack**：建议开发者应优先针对SteamOS API进行开发，以确保与Windows的兼容性，并最大化性能。还提出了使用Rust构建跨平台游戏的设想。
• **Runako**：从个人经验出发，认为Arch Linux上的游戏体验经过适当调整后非常不错，且不打算回到Windows。
• **Lenerdenator**：表示正在等待Linux和GPU驱动的进一步成熟，计划在未来构建PC用于Linux gaming，但目前主要使用Mac，且对UNIX类系统有偏好。
• **Andreldm**：赞扬Valve对Linux gaming的贡献，但提到由于Steam的bug（每天重复下载shader cache）不得不切换回Windows，问题多年未解决。
• **Self-Perfection**：提到在使用Wine运行Windows游戏时，某些情况下性能优于原生Windows，不解其原因。
• **Schmorptron**：认为性能提升可能与DXVK（DirectX到Vulkan的转换层）的优秀表现有关。
• **Pier25**：对Proton带来的性能差异感到惊讶，建议微软发布一个无臃肿软件的Windows游戏版本。
• **Flohofwoe**：认为性能对比可能是因为Linux系统垂直整合更好，而Windows驱动质量参差不齐。还提到Proton团队水平高，可能为某些游戏提供了比原生D3D更好的优化。
• **FlaminHotSpeedo**：质疑文章中关于SteamOS性能优于Windows的结论，认为缺乏数据支持，且文章方法论有问题。
• **Melatonic**：提到Windows 11臃肿的问题，建议使用Windows LTSC版本作为优化的游戏系统，并担心未来游戏和驱动对LTSC的支持。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Linux与Windows在游戏性能上的实际对比，特别是Proton和原生Windows的表现。
• 另一个讨论点是Windows系统的臃肿问题，以及是否存在更优的Windows版本（如LTSC）用于游戏。
• 最后，反作弊支持被认为是Linux gaming普及的一个主要障碍。

Nearly a decade ago, Ars testing found that Valve's
"Steam Machines"-era
version of SteamOS
performed significantly worse than Windows
when SteamOS's Linux game ports were tested on the same hardware as their Windows counterparts. Today, though, Ars testing on the Lenovo Legion Go S finds recent games generally run at higher frame rates on SteamOS 3.7 than on Windows 11. The performance advantage is yet another way that Valve's upstart OS is differentiating itself from the "default" Windows installation used by most PC gamers for decades now.
While users have been able to install Windows on the Steam Deck since its 2022 launch, Valve
doesn't offer official "Windows on Deck" support
for this alternative hardware use case. Lenovo's Legion Go S, on the other hand, is the first gaming portable
explicitly designed to work
with either Windows 11 (in hardware first released in January) or SteamOS (in hardware first released in May, alongside
a new version of SteamOS
designed for non-Valve AMD hardware).
To test the performance impact of this operating system choice, we started with the SteamOS version of the Legion Go S (provided by Lenovo) and tested five high-end 3D games released in the last five years using built-in benchmarking tools and two different graphics/resolution tiers. We then
installed Windows 11 on the handheld
, downloaded
updated drivers from Lenovo's support site
, and re-ran the benchmarks on the same games downloaded through Steam for Windows.

44381144.article_summary: Ars Technica的测试显示，在Lenovo Legion Go S上，SteamOS 3.7的游戏帧率表现普遍优于Windows 11，这在大多数高画质游戏中尤为明显。测试的五款游戏中，有四款在SteamOS上表现出更高的帧率，仅《Borderlands 3》在Windows上略胜一筹。特别是在低画质设置下，操作系统的选择可能决定游戏是否流畅运行。尽管Windows需要通过额外安装Asus提供的非官方驱动才能接近SteamOS的性能，但在多数情况下，Windows的帧率仍比SteamOS低8%到36%。SteamOS通过Proton翻译层实现的高效兼容性，使其在游戏性能上超越了传统Windows系统。

data.article_summary: 2025年5月中旬，Cloudflare成功阻止了一次创纪录的7.3 Tbps DDoS攻击，这是有史以来最大的此类攻击。攻击针对一家使用Cloudflare Magic Transit服务的托管服务提供商，总流量达37.4 TB，在45秒内完成。攻击主要是UDP洪水攻击，伴随少量其他类型的反射和放大攻击。Cloudflare的系统自动检测并缓解了这次攻击，保护了客户免受影响。文章还详细介绍了UDP、QOTD和Echo等攻击类型的原理及防御措施，强调了云基防护的重要性。

In mid-May 2025, Cloudflare blocked the largest DDoS attack ever recorded: a staggering 7.3 terabits per second (Tbps). This comes shortly after the publication of our
DDoS threat report for 2025 Q1
on April 27, 2025, where we highlighted attacks reaching 6.5 Tbps and 4.8 billion packets per second (pps). The 7.3 Tbps attack is 12% larger than our previous record and 1 Tbps greater than a recent attack reported by cyber security reporter Brian Krebs at
KrebsOnSecurity
.
New world record: 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack autonomously blocked by Cloudflare
The attack targeted a Cloudflare customer, a hosting provider, that uses
Magic Transit
to defend their IP network. Hosting providers and critical Internet infrastructure have increasingly become targets of DDoS attacks, as we reported in our
latest DDoS threat report
. Pictured below is an attack campaign from January and February 2025 that blasted over 13.5 million DDoS attacks against Cloudflareâs infrastructure and hosting providers protected by Cloudflare.
DDoS attack campaign target Cloudflare infrastructure and hosting providers protected by Cloudflare
Let's start with some stats, and then weâll dive into how our systems detected and mitigated this attack.
The 7.3 Tbps attack delivered 37.4 terabytes in 45 seconds
37.4 terabytes is not a staggering figure in todayâs scales, but blasting 37.4 terabytes in just 45 seconds is. Itâs the equivalent to flooding your network with over 9,350 full-length HD movies, or streaming 7,480 hours of high-definition video nonstop (thatâs nearly a year of back-to-back binge-watching) in just 45 seconds. If it were music, youâd be downloading about 9.35 million songs in under a minute, enough to keep a listener busy for 57 years straight. Think of snapping 12.5 million high-resolution photos on your smartphone and never running out of storageâeven if you took one shot every day, youâd be clicking away for 4,000 years â but in 45 seconds.Â
The record-breaking 7.3 Tbps DDoS attack delivered 37.4 TB in 45 seconds
The attack details
The attack carpet-bombed an average of 21,925 destination ports of a single IP address owned and used by our customer, with a peak of 34,517 destination ports per second. The attack also originated from a similar distribution of source ports.Â
Distribution of destination ports
Attack vectors
The 7.3 Tbps attack was a multivector DDoS attack. Around 99.996% of the attack traffic was categorized as UDP floods. However, the remaining 0.004%, which accounted for 1.3 GB of the attack traffic, were identified as QOTD reflection attacks, Echo reflection attack, NTP reflection attack, Mirai UDP flood attack, Portmap flood, and RIPv1 amplification attacks.
The attack vectors other than UDP floods
Breakdown of the attack vectors
Below are details about the various attack vectors seen in this attack, how organizations can avoid becoming a reflection and amplification participant, and recommendations on how to defend against these attacks whilst avoiding impact to legitimate traffic. Cloudflare's customers are protected against these attacks.
UDP DDoS attack
Type
: Flood
How it works:
A high volume of UDP packets is sent to random or specific ports on the target IP address(es). It may attempt to saturate the Internet link or overwhelm its in-line appliances with more packets than it can handle.
How to defend against the attack:
Deploy cloud-based volumetric DDoS protection, apply smart rate-limiting on UDP traffic, and drop unwanted UDP traffic altogether.
How to avoid unintended impact:
Aggressive filtering may disrupt legitimate UDP services such as VoIP, video conferencing, or online games. Apply thresholds carefully.
QOTD DDoS attack
Type:
Reflection + Amplification
How it works:
Abuses the Quote of the Day (QOTD) Protocol, which listens on UDP port 17 and responds with a short quote or message. Attackers send QOTD requests to exposed servers from a spoofed IP address, causing amplified responses to flood the victim.
How to prevent becoming a reflection / amplification element:
Disable the QOTD service and block UDP/17 on all servers and firewalls.
How to defend against the attack:
Block inbound UDP/17. Drop abnormal small-packet UDP request spikes.
How to avoid unintended impact:
QOTD is an obsolete diagnostic/debugging protocol and is not used by modern applications. Disabling it should not have any negative effect on legitimate services.
Echo DDoS attack
Type:
Reflection + Amplification
How it works:
Exploits the Echo protocol (UDP/TCP port 7), which replies with the same data it receives. Attackers spoof the victimâs IP address, causing devices to reflect the data back, amplifying the attack.

data.title: XSLT
data.author: _kush
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用XML和XSLT构建静态网站的简单方法，旨在去除复杂的前端构建系统。作者希望用纯HTML和CSS创建网站，但不想手写大量HTML，因此探索了XSLT（可扩展样式表转换语言）。XSLT可以将XML数据转换为HTML，支持循环、变量等功能，且无需JavaScript即可运行于所有 web 浏览器中。作者通过实践发现，使用浏览器作为"客户端"构建系统，可以直接打开XML文件并应用XSLT样式表生成HTML页面。这种方法简化了静态网站的构建，特别适合不想使用现代复杂框架的开发者。虽然XSLT不是万能的，但它为简化Web开发提供了一种有效工具。

44393817.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用XML和XSLT构建静态网站的简单方法，旨在去除复杂的前端构建系统。作者希望用纯HTML和CSS创建网站，但不想手写大量HTML，因此探索了XSLT（可扩展样式表转换语言）。XSLT可以将XML数据转换为HTML，支持循环、变量等功能，且无需JavaScript即可运行于所有 web 浏览器中。作者通过实践发现，使用浏览器作为"客户端"构建系统，可以直接打开XML文件并应用XSLT样式表生成HTML页面。这种方法简化了静态网站的构建，特别适合不想使用现代复杂框架的开发者。虽然XSLT不是万能的，但它为简化Web开发提供了一种有效工具。

data.title: Biomolecular shifts occur in our 40s and 60s (2024)
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 斯坦福医学研究发现，人体在40多岁和60多岁时会经历两次快速的生物分子和微生物群的显著变化。研究人员分析了25至75岁人群的成千上万种分子和微生物，发现大多数分子和微生物的数量并非逐渐变化，而是在44岁和60岁左右发生剧烈变化。这些变化可能影响健康，例如心血管疾病相关分子在两个时间点显著变化，60岁出头的人群免疫功能相关分子也发生变化。研究还表明，男性和女性都在40多岁时经历这些变化，而不仅限于女性的更年期。这一发现揭示了生物衰老的非线性特征，并可能为未来健康干预提供新方向。

We undergo two periods of rapid change, averaging around age 44 and age 60, according to a Stanford Medicine study.
Ratana21

News
Aging & Geriatrics
August 14, 2024
Massive biomolecular shifts occur in our 40s and 60s, Stanford Medicine researchers find
By Rachel Tompa
Time marches on predictably, but biological aging is anything but constant, according to a new Stanford Medicine study.
Share Article:
Facebook
LinkedIn
Twitter
Email
If it's ever felt like everything in your body is breaking down at once, that might not be your imagination. A new Stanford Medicine study shows that many of our molecules and microorganisms dramatically rise or fall in number during our 40s and 60s.
Researchers assessed many thousands of different molecules in people from age 25 to 75, as well as their microbiomes - the bacteria, viruses and fungi that live inside us and on our skin - and found that the abundance of most molecules and microbes do not shift in a gradual, chronological fashion. Rather, we undergo two periods of rapid change during our life span, averaging around age 44 and age 60. A
paper
describing these findings was published in the journal
Nature Aging
Aug. 14.
"We're not just changing gradually over time; there are some really dramatic changes," said
Michael Snyder
, PhD, professor of genetics and the study's senior author. "It turns out the mid-40s is a time of dramatic change, as is the early 60s. And that's true no matter what class of molecules you look at."
Xiaotao Shen, PhD, a former Stanford Medicine postdoctoral scholar, was the first author of the study. Shen is now an assistant professor at Nanyang Technological University Singapore.
These big changes likely impact our health - the number of molecules related to cardiovascular disease showed significant changes at both time points, and those related to immune function changed in people in their early 60s.
Abrupt changes in number
Snyder, the Stanford W. Ascherman, MD, FACS Professor in Genetics, and his colleagues were inspired to look at the rate of molecular and microbial shifts by the observation that the risk of developing many age-linked diseases does not rise incrementally along with years. For example, risks for Alzheimer's disease and cardiovascular disease rise sharply in older age, compared with a gradual increase in risk for those under 60.
The researchers used data from 108 people they've been following to better understand the biology of aging. Past insights from this same group of study volunteers include the discovery of four distinct "
ageotypes
," showing that people's kidneys, livers, metabolism and immune system age at different rates in different people.
Michael Snyder
The new study analyzed participants who donated blood and other biological samples every few months over the span of several years; the scientists tracked many different kinds of molecules in these samples, including RNA, proteins and metabolites, as well as shifts in the participants' microbiomes. The researchers tracked age-related changes in more than 135,000 different molecules and microbes, for a total of nearly 250 billion distinct data points.
They found that thousands of molecules and microbes undergo shifts in their abundance, either increasing or decreasing - around 81% of all the molecules they studied showed non-linear fluctuations in number, meaning that they changed more at certain ages than other times. When they looked for clusters of molecules with the largest changes in amount, they found these transformations occurred the most in two time periods: when people were in their mid-40s, and when they were in their early 60s.
Although much research has focused on how different molecules increase or decrease as we age and how biological age may differ from chronological age, very few have looked at the rate of biological aging. That so many dramatic changes happen in the early 60s is perhaps not surprising, Snyder said, as many age-related disease risks and other age-related phenomena are known to increase at that point in life.
The large cluster of changes in the mid-40s was somewhat surprising to the scientists. At first, they assumed that menopause or perimenopause was driving large changes in the women in their study, skewing the whole group. But when they broke out the study group by sex, they found the shift was happening in men in their mid-40s, too.
"This suggests that while menopause or perimenopause may contribute to the changes observed in women in their mid-40s, there are likely other, more significant factors influencing these changes in both men and women. Identifying and studying these factors should be a priority for future research," Shen said.
Changes may influence health and disease risk

data.title: Sailing the fjords like the Vikings yields unexpected insights
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 实验考古学家、瑞典隆德大学的Greer Jarrett过去三年乘坐着类似维京人的敞篷船，沿已知的维京贸易路线航行了超过5000公里。他通过实践研究，不仅深入了解了这些船只，还发现了挪威沿海的四个可能避风港，这些港口可能属于一个去中心化的网络，在维京时期的贸易和旅行中起到了关键作用。Jarrett使用的是19世纪和20世纪初的挪威传统船只复制品，虽然有同事批评时间跨度太大，但他认为造船技术的延续性使得这种类比是合理的。他的研究填补了维京航行历史中的一些空白，因为关于维京航海的直接史料非常稀少。

不同观点：
• **Divbzero 的观点**：支持通过实验考古学来理解金字塔的建造方法。他提到了一个名为《This Old Pyramid》的NOVA节目，该节目通过实际建造金字塔来探索古埃及人可能使用的技术。这表明他认可通过实践和实验来重现历史建筑过程的价值。

• **Liquix 的观点**：Liquix 以一种幽默且略带讽刺的口吻提到了一种极端的实验方法，即某人用自己的冷冻粪便制作简易刀具，并尝试切割猪皮、肌肉和肌腱，结果失败了。这暗示他对某些实验考古学中的极端或不切实际的实验方法持怀疑态度，可能认为这些方法过于荒谬或不科学。

补充讨论：
• **实验考古学的有效性**：Divbzero 通过引用具体的电视节目支持实验考古学作为理解历史建筑技术的手段，而Liquix 则用一个荒诞的实验例子来质疑某些实验的合理性和可行性。

• **争议焦点**：实验考古学中实验方法的合理性和科学性。Divbzero 强调其教育和探索价值，而Liquix 则通过极端例子指出某些实验可能缺乏实际意义或科学严谨性。

• **论据和例子**：
  - Divbzero 提供了具体的电视节目《This Old Pyramid》作为实验考古学应用的例子。
  - Liquix 则用冷冻粪便刀具实验这个夸张的例子来说明某些实验可能偏离实际，缺乏可行性。

总体而言，讨论围绕实验考古学的价值和合理性展开，其中包含了对具体实验方法的正面支持和幽默批评。

Experimental archaeologist Greer Jarrett of Lund University in Sweden has been sailing in the footsteps of Vikings for the last three years.
If you want to learn more about how and where the
Vikings sailed
, making the journey through the fjords yourself in replica boats is a practical, hands-on approach to achieving that end. Greer Jarrett, an archaeologist at Lund University in Sweden, has spent the last three years doing just that, sailing more than 5,000 kilometers along known Viking trade routes in open, spare-rigged clinker boats similar to those used by the Vikings.
Not only has Jarrett learned a great deal about the boats themselves, he also identified four possible havens along the Norwegian coast, part of what may have been a decentralized network that played a crucial role in trade and travel during that period. And those ports are located farther out to sea than other major ports and hubs known to date, according to
a paper
he published in the Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory.
It's just the latest intriguing discovery enabled by the growing field of experimental archaeology, whereby researchers seek to reverse-engineer all manner of ancient technologies. Experimental archaeologists have, for instance,
built their own versions
of Early Upper Paleolithic adzes, axes, and chisels. The resulting fractures and wear enabled them to develop new criteria for identifying the likely functions of ancient tools. Others have tried to
cook like
the Neanderthals,
concluding that
flint flakes were surprisingly effective for butchering birds, and that roasting the birds damages the bones to such an extent that it's unlikely they would be preserved in the archaeological record.
Kent State University's
Metin Eren
has conducted practical experiments to study, for instance, the trajectories of atlatls attached to spears tipped with replica Clovis points, and how their performance compares to javelins used by Neanderthals. He even
fashioned rudimentary blades
out of his own frozen feces to test whether they could cut through pig hide, muscle, and tendon—solely to test a famous anthropological legend about an elderly Inuit man in the 1950s who purportedly did the same to kill and skin a dog, using its rib cage as a makeshift sled to venture off into the Arctic. (It did not work, so myth: busted. But it did snag Eren an
Ig Nobel prize
.)
Taking a hands-on, experimental archaeological approach to studying the Vikings makes sense in light of the dearth of contemporary written sources. "We have a few things written by outsiders, but there's very, very few accounts written or delivered by people from Scandinavia during that period," Jarrett told Ars. "We normally rely on indirect forms of evidence, be that genetics or archaeology or linguistics, which show strong, very frequent connections across maritime areas in the North Atlantic. But because traveling by boat is kind of an archaeologically invisible act, you don't leave any footprints. So we have very little information about the voyages between these points."
The sailing voyages made by Greer Jarrett during the research project, as well as the four possible Viking harbors he identified.
Credit:
Greer Jarrett
Garrett and his crew used four or five different replica boats for their test voyages. Most were built by volunteers, enthusiasts, or students Jarrett had met during his considerable time in the field. They then sailed along the west coast of the Scandinavian Peninsula, a core area of Viking seafaring.
"These are reconstructions of traditional Norwegian boats from the 1800s and early 1900s," said Jarrett. "My idea was, because of this really long-term continuity in traditional boat building practices, especially in Norway, it might be possible to use these later boats which have lots of similarities to try and work out the potentials of where people might have gotten out. It's the idea of suggesting potentials based on practical experience to try and join those dots between the different evidence we have across the Viking world."
That decision has led to some criticism from colleagues because of the enormous gap in time, but Jarrett defends his choice. "The Viking Age ends in the 11th century, and we're talking about boats from 800 years later," he said. "But the construction techniques and the way they are rigged and their general performance characteristics are similar enough. Because this is a project about voyages and not a project about boat building, it seemed like a defensible analogy."

data.title: Bogong moths use a stellar compass for long-distance navigation at night
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 博贡蛾（*Agrotis infusa*）每年春天从澳大利亚东南部迁徙至澳大利亚阿尔卑斯山的凉爽洞穴，距离可达1000公里。它们依靠夜间的星光作为罗盘，在无月光的夜空下，即使地磁场被中和，仍能朝着适当的迁徙方向飞行。研究发现，这些蛾类的大脑视觉神经元对夜空旋转有特定反应，并调整至共同的天空方向，当蛾朝南飞行时，神经元活动最为活跃。这表明博贡蛾利用星象线索和地球磁场建立了一个强大的罗盘系统，用于长距离夜间导航，以到达特定目的地。秋季时，它们会返回出生地繁殖并死亡。
